name: Business Ethics
description: An interdisciplinary approach to the analysis of ethical problems and issues arising from management and administrative practices in the private and public sector. Among the topics/issues covered will be relationship of ethics and philosophy, sociology, economics, law and management; code of ethics for students of management, economics and political sciences; honesty and social responsibility in management, health and safety in the workplace, discrimination and employment, ethical leadership, impact of marketing operations, misleading and deceiving advertising, product information and promotion, consumer protection, disadvantaged consumers ecological conscientiousness.

name: Critical Reading
description: Developing the skills necessary for a critical approach to texts in English, comprehending the ideas and values stated or implied, comparing the writers' ideas with one's own. Underlying concepts and principles of critical language awareness theory.

name: Critical Reading II
description: Development of reading and interpretive skills. Methods of discourse analysis. Narrative structures and mediation, social context, and privileged positions.

name: English for Philosophy I
description: Understanding of English through works of philosophy and literature. Improving reading, comprehension and writing skills.

name: English for Philosophy II
description: Enhancing spoken and written performance through classroom discussions and reaction papers concerning literary works on the background of philosophy.

name: Language of Social Thought
description: Thematically related readings from 'fundamental' texts in social and economic thought. Examination of formal aspects of presentation and argumentation.

name: English Through Dramatic Text I
description: Proficiency in English reading comprehension through examples from the theater and instructive texts. Deeper awareness of language usage through emphasis on the shared components in the readings.

name: Special Topics: The Utopian Impulse
description: Exploring the imaginary territories known as utopian and dystopian. Examining utopian / dystopian works as presentations of imagined societies, as critical representations of existing societies, and as historical products reflecting the interactions of change and culture.

name: Special Topics: Language and Humor: Critical Readings in a Genre
description: In this course we will explore humor as a tool for understanding the workings of language and culture. As we examine different theories of humor, we will focus on the differences between comedy, laughter and humor, and reflect on the philosophical, psychological and cultural aspects of a subject that has dominated human thought.

name: Survey of American Lit. from 17th-19th Century
description: A chronological survey of American literature from the 17th to the late 19th century, with consideration of eras, movements and individual authors in a cultural and historical settings.

name: Survey of American Literature from Late 19th Century to Present
description: A chronological survey of American literature from the late 19th century to the present, with consideration of works, authors, forms, conventions, ideas, and movements in their cultural and historical settings.

name: Special Topics: In American Literature
description: Intensive study of a theme, movement, genre or author having special significance in American literary history.

name: Elementary Arabic I
description: Introduction to Modern Standard Arabic (MSA). Focus on reading and writing the Arabic alphabet, developing basic vocabulary, and forming simple sentence structures.

name: Elementary Arabic II
prerequisites: ARB 101 or consent of the instructor
description: Reinforcement of basic grammatical structures, verb conjugations in present and past tense, and expansion of vocabulary. Introduction to short texts and basic dialogues.

name: Pre-Intermediate Arabic I
prerequisites: ARB 102 or consent of the instructor
description: Further development of grammatical knowledge including nominal sentences, dual and plural forms, root-based vocabulary building, and verb patterns. Emphasis on oral and written expression.

name: Pre-Intermediate Arabic II
prerequisites: ARB 201 or consent of the instructor
description: Introduction to complex sentence structures such as conditionals and relative clauses. Reading and discussion of short informative texts.

name: Intermediate Arabic I
prerequisites: ARB 202 or consent of the instructor
description: Consolidation of key grammatical structures. Introduction to derived verb forms.

name: Intermediate Arabic II
prerequisites: ARB 301 or consent of the instructor
description: Development of comprehension and production of longer texts. Introduction to idiomatic expressions, connectors, and discourse markers.

name: Arabic-Turkish Translation I
prerequisites: ARB 302 or consent of the instructor
description: Introduction to the theory and practice of Arabic-Turkish translation. Analysis of syntactic and semantic features in both languages.

name: Arabic-Turkish Translation II
prerequisites: ARB 401 or consent of the instructor
description: Advanced translation practice involving journalistic, academic, and literary texts. Focus on stylistic adaptation, terminology, and cultural equivalence.

name: Arabic for the Press
prerequisites: ARB 302 or consent of the instructor
description: Exploration of contemporary media Arabic, including vocabulary and structures common in newspapers, news websites, and political commentary. Focus on journalistic style, headline structure, and editorial expressions.

name: Arabic Literary Texts
prerequisites: ARB 302 or consent of the instructor
description: Reading and discussion of selected modern and classical Arabic literary works (poetry and prose). Emphasis on stylistic analysis, rhetorical devices, and literary genres.

name: Arab Culture and History
prerequisites: ARB 302 or consent of the instructor
description: A cultural and historical overview of the Arab world from pre-Islamic times to the modern era. Topics including religion, society, language development, and cultural production, supplemented by authentic materials in Arabic.

name: Modern Arabic Literature
prerequisites: ARB 421 or consent of the instructor
description: Survey of major themes, authors, and movements in 20th and 21st-century Arabic literature. Selected readings of translated and original Arabic texts with glosses.

name: Armenian for Beginners I
description: An introductory course in modern Western Armenian: the Armenian alphabet, elementary vocabulary and simple grammatical forms. Elementary readings.

name: Armenian for Beginners II
prerequisites: ARM 101 or consent of the instructor
description: Basic knowledge of vocabulary, grammar and syntax. Readings of selected passages of Armenian texts.

name: Introduction to American Studies
description: An interdisciplinary survey of American culture; Its touching on history, government, literature and the arts. Reading of culturally significant texts.

name: Historiography
description: Fundamentals of historical theory and historical scholarship in the twentieth century. Review of the methods of major historians relevant to modern Turkish history.

name: Legal Reforms in Turkish History
description: The classical Ottoman legal system, the Tanzimat reforms, the dichotomies and parallel institutions of the 19th century, whether or the extent to which the Second Constitutional Period approximated the creation of a secular state, and the culmination of this process in the Republican 1920s and 30s. Questions of law and legality during the war years.

name: Economic & Social History of Turkey
description: Changing world-contexts for the Turkish economy from the Tanzimat era to the present, and within that matrix, the unfolding connections of economic growth, structural change, income distribution, and social transformation. The emergence of new social groups and strata during the 19th and 20th centuries.

name: EC. & Soc. Hist.of the Mid.east Since 1800
description: A survey of European economic penetration and the varieties of local response until World War I; and the rise of nation-states and national economies after 1918, including their implications for social change and the emergence of new social groups or strata. With particular emphasis on comparisons between the experience of Anatolia/Turkey and other parts of the region.

name: Foreign Policy of the Republic
description: The implications of Turkey's geographical position; her relations with Great Powers in the 19th century, and the influence of these relations on Ottoman foreign policy; Ataturk's efforts to formulate a distinct Republican foreign policy in the light of past experience; Turkey and the League of Nations in the interwar era; the system of alliances established that Ataturk sought to forge in the 1920s and 30s in order to create peace zones around Turkey; the precarious and ambivalent neutrality of 1939-45; the main axes of Turkish foreign policy during the Cold War. The emerging quests and orientations of the post-cold war era.

name: History of the Middle East
description: Themes and problems in Middle Eastern history particularly relevant to the history of nineteenth century Ottoman Empire and Republican Turkey.

name: History of Eastern Europe
description: Historical survey and analysis of political, social and economic changes which shaped Eastern Europe in the 19th and 20th centuries. Emphasis on the interwar period (1918-1939).

name: Guided Research in Turkish History II
description: Empirical and comparative readings and research assignments on various topics in Modern Turkish History based on students' research projects. Supervision of the progress of research projects by thesis advisors.

name: Selected Topics: In Soci.theory & HIST.
description: An interdisciplinary seminar designed to provide students with theoretical approaches to the study of history. The specific subjects treated in this seminar will vary according to student needs and instructor interest.

name: Selected Topics: In Social Theory & History
description: An interdisciplinary seminar designed to provide students with theoretical approaches to the study of history. The specific subjects treated in this seminar will vary according to student needs and instructor interest.

name: Selected Topics: In Economy and Society in Turkey
description: A comprehensive analysis of cultural history in modern Turkey with focus on the impact of culture on Turkish society. Primary source readings of journals, newspapers, and monographs (in English and/or Turkish) regarding the cultural history of Turkey complemented with a general discussion on culture in recent historiographical literature.

name: Selected Topics: In Turkish Political Thought
description: A systematic and detailed analysis of Turkish political thought from the late nineteenth century to the present. The interactions between political thinkers and political leaders together with an introductory discussion on the developments in political thought elsewhere in the world.

name: Topics in the Hist.of the Modern World
description: Intensive readings and group discussions on selected topics in comparative world history. The specific topics treated in this course will vary according to student needs and instructor interest.

name: Special Topics: In Modern History
description: An advanced special topics course examining In Modern History.

name: Elementary Laz I
description: Introduction to the sound system, elementary vocabulary and simple grammatical forms of Laz. Mastery of the Laz alphabet.

name: Elementary Laz II
prerequisites: CAU 101 or consent of the instructor
description: Basic knowledge of vocabulary, grammar and syntax of Laz. Equal emphasis on reading, writing, speaking and listening skills.

name: Elementary Kabardian I
description: Introduction to the sound system, basic vocabulary and grammatical structures of Kabardian. Kabardian alphabet.

name: Elementary Kabardian II
prerequisites: CAU 111 or consent of the instructor
description: Basic knowledge of vocabulary, grammar and syntax of Kabardian. Equal emphasis on reading, writing, speaking and listening skills.

name: Elementary Abkhaz I
description: Introduction to the sound system, basic vocabulary and grammatical structures of Abkhaz. Abkhaz alphabet.

name: Elementary Abkhaz II
prerequisites: CAU 121 or consent of the instructor
description: Basic knowledge of vocabulary, grammar and syntax of Abkhaz. Equal emphasis on reading, writing, speaking and listening skills.

name: Intermediate Laz I
prerequisites: CAU 102 or consent of the instructor
description: Detailed analysis of Laz grammar. Further development of oral and written use of the language with emphasis on vocabulary expansion.

name: Intermediate Laz II
prerequisites: CAU 201 or consent of the instructor
description: Comprehensive overview of grammatical points introduced in CAU 201. Enhancement of reading, writing, listening and speaking skills and the use of complex sentence structure.

name: Intermediate Kabardian I
prerequisites: CAU 112 or consent of the instructor
description: Detailed analysis of Kabardian grammar. Further development of oral and written use of the language with emphasis on vocabulary expansion.

name: Intermediate Kabardian II
prerequisites: CAU 211 or consent of the instructor
description: Comprehensive overview of grammatical points introduced in CAU 211. Enhancement of reading, writing, listening and speaking skills and the use of complex sentence structure.

name: Intermediate Abkhaz I
prerequisites: CAU 122 or consent of the instructor
description: Detailed analysis of Abkhaz grammar. Further development of oral and written use of the language with emphasis on vocabulary expansion.

name: Intermediate Abkhaz II
prerequisites: CAU 221 or consent of the instructor
description: Comprehensive overview of grammatical points introduced in CAU 221. Enhancement of reading, writing, listening and speaking skills and the use of complex sentence structure.

name: Advanced Laz I
prerequisites: CAU 202 or consent of the instructor
description: Introduction to Laz literature and culture through literary texts and print media. Development of more advanced writing and speakingskills in a variety of discourse genres and reinforcement of complex grammatical structures.

name: Advanced Laz II
prerequisites: CAU 301 or consent of the instructor
description: Focus on the reading and discussion of selected literary texts in Laz. Further enhancement of writing and speaking skills and expansion of vocabulary through literary texts and print media.

name: Advanced Kabardian I
prerequisites: CAU 212 or consent of the instructor
description: Introduction to Kabardian literature and culture through literary texts and print media. Development of more advanced writing and speaking skills in a variety of discourse genres and reinforcement of complex grammatical structures.

name: Advanced Kabardian II
prerequisites: CAU 311 or consent of the instructor
description: Focus on the reading and discussion of selected literary texts in Kabardian. Further enhancement of writing and speaking skills and expansion of vocabulary through literary texts and print media.

name: Advanced Abkhaz I
prerequisites: CAU 222 or consent of the instructor
description: Introduction to Abkhaz literature and culture through literary texts and print media. Development of more advanced writing and speakingskills in a variety of discourse genres and reinforcement of complex grammatical structures.

name: Advanced Abkhaz II
prerequisites: CAU 321 or consent of the instructor
description: Focus on the reading and discussion of selected literary texts in Abkhaz. Further enhancement of writing and speaking skills and expansion of vocabulary through literary texts and print media.

name: Beginners Chinese I
description: Emphasis on intensive reading, conversation and simple sentence structures in grammar. Listening, writing, and introduction to 100 ideograms.

name: Beginners Chinese II
prerequisites: CHIN 101 or consent of the instructor
description: Emphasis on intensive reading, conversation and grammar. Listening, writing, and another 100 ideograms.

name: Intermediate Chinese I
prerequisites: CHIN 102 or consent of the instructor
description: Emphasis on reading and complex structures in grammar. Conversation and additional 200 ideograms.

name: Intermediate Chinese II
prerequisites: CHIN 201 or consent of the instructor
description: Emphasis on reading and more complex structures in grammar. Conversation and additional 200 ideograms.

name: Advanced Chinese I
prerequisites: CHIN 202 or consent of the instructor
description: Reading, grammar, conversation, and writing at advanced level. Introduction to readings in Chinese culture.

name: Advanced Chinese II
prerequisites: CHIN 301 or consent of the instructor
description: Extending reading, grammar, conversation, and writing at advanced level. Readings in Chinese culture.

name: Readings in Chinese Culture I
prerequisites: CHIN 302 or consent of the instructor
description: Reading, grammar, conversation and writing. Advanced readings in Chinese history and culture.

name: Readings in Chinese Culture II
prerequisites: CHIN 401 or consent of the instructor
description: Reading, grammar, translation according to Chinese ability. Readings in classical Chinese literature.

name: Classical Literature
description: A survey of major works of ancient Greek and Roman literature in translation, with emphasis on the structural and thematic features of epic, lyric and dramatic poetry.

name: Literary Theory and Criticism I
description: Analysis of the most significant theoretical statements on literature prior to the modern period, focusing on major critical works from the Classical (Greek, Hellenistic, Roman), Medieval, and Early Modern periods, ending with Neoclassical criticism and aesthetic theory.

name: Literary Theory and Criticism II
description: Selected critical works of European Romanticism; the foundational figures of modern criticism (Marx, Nietzsche, Freud, Heidegger, Saussure); the rise of structuralism; and the emergence of critical methodologies based in identity politics, from feminism to theories of race and ethnicity.

name: Literary Theory and Criticism III
description: A survey of the most significant moments in modern and contemporary literary theory. Deconstruction, cultural studies, and the rise of post-structuralist, post-Marxist, post psychoanalytic, and post colonial theory.

name: Literary Theory & Criticism III
description: A survey of the most significant moments in modern and contemporary literary theory. Deconstruction, cultural studies, and the rise of post-structuralist, post-Marxist, post psychoanalytic, and post colonial theory.

name: Contemporary Trends in Literature
description: A study of contemporary Anglo-American texts written during the last two decades of the 20th century and the 21st century as challenges to conventional understanding of genres and in interactions with current critical theories.

name: Analysis of Poetry
description: Seminar in poetry, with special attention to contemporary aesthetics and textual criticism. Practical application of stylistics and of other modes of analysis to selected works.

name: Special Topics: In Comparative Literature
description: Intensive study of a particular mode, genre or movement with examples selected from several cultures and literary periods. Topics vary from year to year.

name: Special Topics: Literature and the Arts
description: This course is focused on the relationship of literature to the arts, such as painting, music and dance, both in content and form. In the introductory part of the course, we will revisit critics and poets from the classical period onwards, such as Cicero, Horace, Dante, Kant, and Borges, just to name a few, through short but crucial excerpts from their works concerned with the specificities of verbal and visual forms of representation (of truth and/or beauty),.

name: Special Topics: Mythmaking in Women's Poetry
description: An advanced special topics course examining Mythmaking in Women's Poetry.

name: Special Topics: Ecopoetics
description: Ecopoetics is the study of the collusion of poetry and nature, a very old and now mainstream approach to current debates in environmental studies in the Humanities. This class will begin with a focus on some fundamental notions that inform ecopoetical discourse.

name: Special Topics: Postcolonial Ecologies
description: Intensive study of a particular mode, genre or movement with examples selected from several cultures and literary periods. Topics vary from year to year.

name: Special Topics: Fiction, Film and Psychoanalysis
description: An advanced special topics course examining Fiction, Film and Psychoanalysis.

name: Special Topics: Spectrality
description: This course examines spectrality—a critical approach emerging in the 1990s that analyzes ghostly presences in literature and theory. Specters, ghosts, revenants, and phantoms are approached not as literal phenomena, but as conceptual metaphors that reveal absent presences.

name: Special Topics: Feminism & Poetry
description: Intensive study of a particular mode, genre or movement with examples selected from several cultures and literary periods. Topics vary from year to year.

name: Special Topics: Aesthetic Encounters
description: Intensive study of a particular mode, genre or movement with examples selected from several cultures and literary periods. Topics vary from year to year.

name: Special Topics: Postcolonial Literatures
description: An advanced special topics course examining Postcolonial Literatures.

name: Special Topics: Fictions of Crime
description: An advanced special topics course examining Fictions of Crime.

name: Special Topics: Love in Western Literature
description: This course explores the theme of love in Western literature, from the epics of Ancient Greece to modern poetry and prose. Through a historical and philosophical lens, students will examine the literary constructions and social implications of love in various forms—romantic, platonic, familial, friendly, and divine.

name: Special Topics: Poetic Geographies of Divided Cities
description: This course focuses on the comparative relationships among short literature, material, and urban space. Namely, by focusing on three cities—Chicago, Berlin and Istanbul— this course explores how twentieth and twenty-first century literature both represents urban space but also appears as short genres in the streets, on walls, public signs, trains, and other material locations.

name: Special Topics: Precarity in Contemporary Fiction
description: In this course, we will engage with representations of precarity in the twenty-first-century (Anglo-American) fiction. We will examine the notion both as an ontological condition of humanity and as the predominant politico-economic phenomenon of the twenty-first century afflicting humans and nonhumans alike with systemic injustices and exploitations.

name: Postcolonial Theory and Literature: Politics and Aesthetics of Representation
description: An elective course exploring Postcolonial Theory and Literature: Politics and Aesthetics of Representation.

name: Special Topics: Genealogy of Emotions in Western Literature
description: An advanced special topics course examining Genealogy of Emotions in Western Literature.

name: Special Topics: Time & Space in Narrative
description: With special attention to theories of time and space in/of narrative by Gaston Bachelard, Mieke Bal, Mikhail Bakhtin, Walter Benjamin, Pierre Bourdieu, Ursula Heise, Henri Lefebvre and Paul Ricoeur, among others, this course will focus on shifting and multiplying perceptions and conceptions of time, space, and place, as well as of reality, society, and subjectivity, as they find expression in contemporary fiction.

name: Special Topics: Anger & Masculinity in Postwar British Literature
description: This course examines British postwar literature (1950-1960), often referred to by critics as the “Angry Young Men (and Women)”. You will read two plays and two novels against the backdrop of Britain’s expanding welfare state, shifting class structures, and debates about education after World War II.

name: Special Topics: Contemporary Dystopian Fiction
description: Intensive study of a particular mode, genre or movement with examples selected from several cultures and literary periods. Topics vary from year to year.

name: Special Topics: Travel Writing and Empire
description: An advanced special topics course examining Travel Writing and Empire.

name: Special Topics: On the Sublime
description: An advanced special topics course examining On the Sublime.

name: Special Topics: Contemporary Fiction
description: An advanced special topics course examining Contemporary Fiction.

name: American Drama
description: A study of American drama, with special emphasis on the works of Eugene O'Neill, Arthur Miller and Tennessee Williams.

name: Modern Drama
description: Extensive reading and discussion of modern drama beginning with Ibsen and including the chief British and European dramatists of our day.

name: Principles of Microeconomics
description: Nature, scope and methods of economics; a general view of the price system; consumer behavior; theory of the firm; illustrations and applications from the Turkish economy.

name: Principles of Macroeconomics
description: National income and its determination; changes in national income, elements of public finance, money and banking, international trade, macroeconomic policy, economic growth and development; illustrations and applications from the Turkish economy.

name: World Economic History
description: Survey of world economic history; theories of long run economic development; discussion of roles of geography, institutions, politics and culture; characteristics of and empirical evidence on different eras; transition to agriculture; Malthusian era; industrialization.

name: Economic Policy
description: Growth and development policy; fiscal policy; monetary policy; labor market policy; open economy and trade issues; political economy of economic policy; redistribution, government regulation and oversight; political aspects of economic policy-making.

name: Environmental & Ecological Economics
description: The development of environmental thinking in economics; alternative definitions and measurements of sustainability; a survey of contemporary economic approaches that conceptualize the economics-environment relationship; environmental valuation; decision-making techniques, costbenefit analysis and multi-criteria evaluation; environmental policy instruments. Case studies.

name: History of Economic Thought
description: The pre-history of classical political economy; forefathers and constitutive debates in the classical political economy. Marx’s challenge and critique; transition from feudalism to capitalism; colonialism; enclosure movement; industrial revolution; the free trade debate; population growth; capitalism and its crises.

name: Topics in History of Economic Thought
description: Constitutive debates and internal divisions in neoclassical economics; the heterodox alternatives to the neoclassical orthodoxy; different notions of actors, knowledge and equilibrium; different explanations of the interactions between markets and states; different theories of market and government failures; different and competing conceptualizations of the role that institutions, power mechanisms and class structures play in shaping social outcomes.

name: Marxian Economics
description: Introduction to Marxian economics; definitions, key concepts and methodology of Marxian economics; modes of production; transition from feudalism to capitalism; labor theory of value; class analysis; capitalism and its crisis tendencies.

name: Turkish Economy
description: The evolution of the structure and institutions of Turkish economy; growth, production, trade and distribution patterns; evolution of economic policy and current economic issues.

name: Growth and Development
description: Concepts and measurement of growth and development; a survey of conventional, non-conventional and critical theories of growth and development; the identification of major problems of economic development and globalisation.

name: Topics in International Development
description: The evolution of the post war international economic order; development strategies and country experiences in a comparative perspective; a survey of leading issues in economic development.

name: Introduction to Education
description: Basic concepts, principles and characteristics of education; social, political, philosophical, and historical foundations of education in general and the Turkish educational system in particular.

name: Social Foundations of Education
description: School as a social institution in a social system. Critical analysis of roles of students, teachers and schools in society.

name: Living with Disabilities
description: Awareness of disabling conditions and identifying differences in oneself and others. Exclusion and disability as a marker of identity.

name: History of Turkish Education
description: Analysis of historical forces influencing the development of Turkish education with a focus on relations between the school and other social institutions.

name: Philosophy of Education
description: Introduction to philosophical foundations of education. Prominent educational philosophers.

name: Educational Psychology
description: Understanding the human potential, effectiveness and motivation. Human development and diversity.

name: Comparative Education
description: Introduction to comparative and international studies in education. Examination of theoretical approaches, contemporary issues, current trends, and major concepts including power, equity, and gender.

name: Education & Social Development
description: Analysis of interaction between education, and social, political and economic development. Examining the means that schools reproduce or challenge the prevailing social, economic and political order.

name: Introduction to Peace Education
description: Introduction to the core concepts and pedagogy of peace education. Discussion of historical and current dimensions of peace education including human rights, social justice, disarmament, intercultural solidarity, environmental care and inner peace.

name: Comparative Experiences in Education
description: Examination of educational issues in different cultural settings. Opportunity to visit related sites of interest and engage in dailogues with policy makers, practitioners, students or administrators.

name: Education and Globalization
description: Critical examination of relations between education and globalization. Review of major debates on educational policy, economy, culture, and politics related to globalization.

name: Organizational Counseling
description: Understanding organizational behavior and introduction to organizational behavior theories and models. Organizational counseling techniques including problem solving, negotiation and conflict resolution, leadership and team building.

name: Special Topics: Social PSY. of Edu
description: This elective course is designed to explore the social psychology of education through a scientific project implemented at two state high schools in Istanbul. The project, titled “D-STEK (Dijitalde ve STEM’de Engelleri Kaldırmak),” aims to understand the reasons and motivations behind high school girls' choices to pursue either science or humanities tracks.

name: Survey of English Literature from Old English Period to Restoration
description: A chronological survey of English literature from Old English times to the Restoration, with consideration of works, authors, forms, conventions, ideas and movements in their historical settings.

name: Survey of English Literature from Restoration to Present
description: A chronological survey of English literature from the 17th century to the present, with consideration of works, authors, forms, conventions, ideas and movements in their historical settings.

name: Medieval English Literature
description: Romances, lyrics, allegories, popular tales read against the social and cultural background of the age, with special emphasis on Chaucer.

name: The English Renaissance
description: A study of the major texts of the English Renaissance from More to Milton with special attention to the development of lyric poetry.

name: Restoration and Augustan Literature
description: A study of poetry, prose, drama, fiction and criticism from 1660 to the end of the 18th Century with emphasis on comedy of manners and the satires of Dryden, Pope and Swift.

name: Studies in Shakespeare
description: In-depth analysis of a few of Shakespeare’s great plays, emphasizing both the poetic and dramatic aspects of his art. Consideration of the historical context and of the varieties of critical interpretation.

name: The English Romantics
description: A study of the major romantic poets and prose writers of the 19th Century, with special emphasis on the aesthetics of Blake, Wordsworth, Coleridge, Byron, Shelley and Keats.

name: Modern Novel
description: Analysis of the examples of modern and contemporary novels from English and world literatures, mostly from the 1900s, with a particular focus on the theory of the novel.

name: Victorian Poetry & Prose
description: A study of the greater Victorian poets and prose writers, with attention to relationships between the literature and the social and intellectual trends of the age.

name: Modern Poetry
description: Analysis of modern and contemporary poetry in English, starting with W.B. Yeats, comprising mainly English and American but including European poets as well. Close examination of the poems in terms of their form and content within their intellectual and cultural contexts, employing diverse methods of literary criticism.

name: Special Topics: Poetry and the Self
description: In this course, through close readings of poems and relative theory to broaden our perspective, we will study various speakers that enable a poet to take different stances concerning the "self" of the poet. By examining the concept of the "self" of the poet in poetry through speakers, we will also touch upon subjectivity as a concept and assess its mpact on the aesthetic quality of an artwork.

name: Introduction to Literary Forms I
description: An introduction to forms of literature and literary and stylistic analysis of texts. Examination of examples of poetry, short story and drama with reference to a wide range of critical principles and interpretative tools.

name: Introduction to Literary Forms II
description: An introduction to the novel as a major literary genre, with reference to a wide range of critical principles and interpretative tools.

name: The Environmental Dimension
description: Introduction to ecology; material and energy cycles; populations and communities; evolution. Major environmental issues facing humanity.

name: Social Ecology
description: Trends and developments in earth's post-industrial revolution environmental history. Introduction to the concepts of ecosystems and their functions.

name: Sustainable Development
description: Principles of sustainable development. Key challanges related to sustainable development such as population growth, environmental resource management, pollution prevention and environmental protection, poverty alleviation, inequality, trade and economic growth.

name: Anatolian Arts & Cultures from Prehistoric Times to the End of the Classical Ages I
description: This is a general survey course intended to introduce students from various disciplines to the cultural and artistic development of Anatolia from prehistoric times (the beginning of Lower Paleolithic) to the end of the lron Age (end of the 6th Century B.C.). The emphasis will be on material remains combined with some historical background.

name: Anatolian Arts & Cultures from Prehistoric Times to the End of the Classical Ages II
description: This is a general survey course intended to introduce students from various disciplines to the cultural and artistic development of Anatolia from the beginning of the Classical Age (5th. Century B.c.) to the end of the Roman period (337 A.D.). The emphasis will be on material remains combined with some historical background.

name: Monumental Structures of Istanbul Through the Ages I
description: This course will be a study of the monuments of lstanbul throughout the city's history, from its founding as the city-state of Byzantium in 667 B.C., through the Archaic, Classical, Hellenistic and Roman Periods, including the era when it was Constantinople, the capital of the Byzantine Empire, until the conquest of the city by Sultan Mehmet II. The course will involve regular field trips to study the monuments of lstanbul and visit the city's museums.

name: Monumental Structures of Istanbul Through the Ages II
description: This course will be the study of the monuments of lstanbul rebuilt by Sultan Mehmet II as the capital of the Ottoman Empire, the development of the city and its monuments in the later periods of the Empire; baroque and rococo Ottoman architecture and the development of lstanbul under the Turkish Republic. The course will involve regular field trips to study the monuments of lstanbul and visit the city's museums.

name: History of Turkish Painting I
description: Discussion of Turkish painting within the context of cultural history: murals, the Turkish Primitives and followers of the Naturalist and lmpressionist.

name: History of Turkish Painting II
description: Discussion of Turkish painting within the context of cultural history: the development of modernist trends in the Republican Era.

name: Western Painting in the Nineteenth Century
description: The development of art movements in the nineteenth century: revival of classicism, gothic, renaissance, baroque, and romanesque. The romantic movement (Goya, Gericault, Delacroix, Constable, Turner, Blake), the Barbizon group in France, the lmpressionists.

name: Western Painting in the Twentieth Century
description: Paul Cezanne, Seurat, Gauguin, Van Gogh; the fauvists, the cubists, the vorticists, the expressionists, and the post-impressionists at large.

name: Art of Our Times: The History & Criticism of Recent International Art I
description: An advanced course which traces the complex developments in painting, sculpture, and new art forms from the 1960's through the present day, including Minimalism, conceptual art, environmental art, performance art, abstract painting, photo realism, "New lmage" painting, new expressionism, and others, with attention to the variety of emerging contemporary regional and national manifestations. The course discusses concepts of contemporary art criticism and develops the student's individual basis of critical judgment.

name: Art of Our Times: The History & Criticism of Recent International Art II
description: An advanced course which traces the complex developments in painting, sculpture, and new art forms from the 1960's through the present day, including Minimalism, conceptual art, environmental art, performance art, abstract painting, photo realism, "New lmage" painting, new expressionism, and others, with attention to the variety of emerging contemporary regional and national manifestations. The course discusses concepts of contemporary art criticism and develops the student's individual basis of critical judgment.

name: A General History of European Painting and Sculpture I
description: An introductory course which traces the dominant art styles and major movements throughout continental Europe, including the Hellenic, Roman, early Christian and Byzantine, Romanesque, Gothic and Renaissance.

name: A General History of European Painting and Sculpture II
description: A continuation of Semester 1, the course covers the high Renaissance, the Baroque, the Rococo, neoclassicism, post-impressionism, cubism and the emergence of abstract art.

name: Museums and Cultural Heritage
description: The development of museums in the West and in Turkey, the significance of their role in protecting and conveying cultural heritage, the problems of collecting and preserving cultural products as well as activities to be carried out by museum administrations, the role of museums in the world, how they are run and special collections in major museums will be studied throughout the course.

name: Music Appreciation I
description: These courses will concentrate on the fundamentals and functions of music in different ages. They will also attempt to study the development of music in relation to other, parallel cultural phenomena.

name: Music Appreciation II
description: These courses will concentrate on the fundamentals and functions of music in different ages. They will also attempt to study the development of music in relation to other, parallel cultural phenomena.

name: Vocal Music Appreciation I
description: This course will attempt to get the student acquainted with various forms of music through the ages with emphasis on vocal music of the Renaissance, baroque, classical and Romantic periods. Many different styles will be covered from early madrigals and motets to the oratorio, opera and contemporary vocal/choral repertoire, together with an introduction to vocal technique, often making use of audio-visual equipment.

name: Vocal Music Appreciation II
description: This course will attempt to get the student acquainted with various forms of music through the ages with emphasis on vocal music of the Renaissance, baroque, classical and Romantic periods. Many different styles will be covered from early madrigals and motets to the oratorio, opera and contemporary vocal/choral repertoire, together with an introduction to vocal technique, often making use of audio-visual equipment.

name: Music: Theory & Appreciation
description: This will be a one semester survey that introduces the logic and aesthetic of written musical theory systems of the modern world. Recorded examples demonstrating also the variety of musical instruments will promote understanding and a subsequent appreciation of value.

name: Twentieth Century Western Classical Music
description: An introduction to the theory of European music; its historical roots; modern expressions and satellite variations will be considered. There will be a concentration on the reading of music, interpreting notes as sound.

name: Comparative Theory of Music and the Arts I
description: The first part of the course will cover the musical ages of medieval, Renaissance, baroque, classical and early romantic periods, and the second part will cover the music of the Romantic period and the twentieth century as well as Turkish music and jazz. The history of music will be offered with examples by audio-visual equipment and occasional lectures by prominent musicians.

name: Comparative Theory of Music and the Arts II
description: The first part of the course will cover the musical ages of medieval, Renaissance, baroque, classical and early romantic periods, and the second part will cover the music of the Romantic period and the twentieth century as well as Turkish music and jazz. The history of music will be offered with examples by audio-visual equipment and occasional lectures by prominent musicians.

name: Music in Turkey
description: An introduction to sacred and secular forms of Turkish folk and classical musics and to various urban popular traditions. Analyses of musical sounds and form together with indigenous concepts of musical theory and performance.

name: Introduction to Music I
description: The study of music by genre rather than chronology. Students are trained in how to listen analytically and are acquainted with a wide variety of musical forms.

name: Introduction to Music II
description: The study of music by genre rather than chronology. Students are trained in how to listen analytically and are acquainted with a wide variety of musical forms.

name: World Popular Music I
description: Survey of popular music from Asia, Europe, the Middle East, the Caribbean and Latin America, subSaharan Africa, and Australia. Using a number of selected case studies, issues raised by popular music, such as the relationship of music to cultural identity, nationalism, urbanism, westernism, and the recording and broadcasting industries will be discussed.

name: World Popular Music II
description: Survey of popular music from Asia, Europe, the Middle East, the Caribbean and Latin America, subSaharan Africa, and Australia. Using a number of selected case studies, issues raised by popular music, such as the relationship of music to cultural identity, nationalism, urbanism, westernism, and the recording and broadcasting industries will be discussed.

name: History of the Cinema
description: Introduction to the major phases of international film history from its origins to the present including screenings and discussion of narrative films, which are representative of film movements, technological innovations and influential directors.

name: Introduction to Film Analysis
description: Introduction to film analysis and criticism, concepts of film style and narrative film genres (documentary, avant-garde, science fiction, gangster, musical etc.).

name: Film Theory
description: Discussions of cinematic language, cinema as art form, as social expression, creativity in an industrial medium; emphasis on major historical positions in classical film theory as well as recent developments.

name: The Art of Dance I
description: An appreciation of dance--both as a traditional and as a modern art form. The development of dance- dance as a basic form of expression, ballet, modern and avant-garde dance--is to be studied, the place of dance in Turkey is to be discussed by way of slides, videos and films.

name: The Art of Dance II
description: An appreciation of dance--both as a traditional and as a modern art form. The development of dance- dance as a basic form of expression, ballet, modern and avant-garde dance--is to be studied, the place of dance in Turkey is to be discussed by way of slides, videos and films.

name: Music of Ottoman Istanbul
description: The musical culture of Istanbul from the Ottoman period to the early Republic. Classical, Sufi, military, and musical traditions in different communities. Understanding the cultural fabric of Ottoman society through music. Key concepts of Turkish music theory.

name: History of Painting and Sculpture in the USA I
description: An advanced course which traces the major movements, manifestations, and historical figures in American art from its beginning in the Colonial Period to the Post-World War il period. it includes Colonial Portraiture, early 19th century landscape, late 19th century adoption of lmpressionism and Post-lmpressionism, the early experiments in Abstraction, Regionalism and Social Protest painting, and emphasizes Abstract Expressionism of the 1940's and 1950's and Pop Art of the 1960's.

description: An advanced course which traces the major movements, manifestations, and historical figures in American art from its beginning in the Colonial Period to the Post-World War il period. it includes Colonial Portraiture, early 19th century landscape, late 19th century adoption of lmpressionism and Post-lmpressionism, the early experiments in Abstraction, Regionalism and Social Protest painting, and emphasizes Abstract Expressionism of the 1940's and 1950's and Pop Art of the 1960's.

description: The course introduces students to the genre of travel writing and its connection to Empire starting from the 16th century. Engaging in close reading of these texts, the course questions the relationship between fact and fiction in travelogues, and the cultural and political ends these narratives have served through the centuries.

name: Special Topics: World Cinema
description: This course will focus on the national and transnational contexts of contemporary cinema as well as historical practices of film production and criticism across these contexts. Discussion of these frameworks alongside other related concepts: genre, industry economics, cross-cultural remakes, festival culture, globalization, media regulation, nationalism, and reception.

name: Film History I: Beginning to 1960
description: The history of world cinema from 1895 to 1960. Major film traditions and technological, economic, and historical conditions, cinematic styles and techniques, thematic and artistic trends, important filmmakers, and notable films that shape them.

name: Film History II: 1960 to Present
description: A survey of the history of world cinema, from 1960 to the present day. Exploration of major film traditions alongside technological, economic, and historical conditions, cinematic styles and techniques, thematic and artistic trends, important filmmakers, and notable films that shape them.

name: Film Analysis
description: Introduction to formal concepts and basic interpretive tools in film analysis, including narrative, mise-en-scène, acting, cinematography, sound, editing, and genre. Exploration of the “grammar” and expressive range of cinematic language and the ways in which complex emotions and ideas are communicated to the viewer.

name: Film Theory
description: A general survey of major currents and debates in classical, modern, and contemporary film theory, including film ontology, medium specificity, realism, formalism, auteur theory, spectatorship theory, film language and semiotics (structuralism), Marxism, apparatus theory and ideology critique, genre theory, psychoanalysis, feminism, poststructuralism, postcolonialism, culturalism, neoformalism, cognitivism, phenomenology, schizoanalysis, hauntology, memory studies, affect theory, ecocriticism, and the philosophy of film amongst others.

name: Screenwriting I: Introduction to Screenwriting
description: Introduction to the fundamentals of screenwriting. Exploration of the basic theories and formal elements of film narrative, including story and plot, setting and scope, theme and tone, character arc and development, conflict and causality, point of view, genre conventions, scene writing, and dialogue.

name: Screenwriting V: Script Analysis
description: A comprehensive study of film scripts from page to screen, with a strong emphasis on the critical analysis of key storytelling elements. Focus on narrative structure, story patterns, thematic depth, tone, setting, character development, conflict, dramatic events, action/reaction cycles, beats, climax, denouement, dialogue, subtext, style, and genre conventions.

name: Making of a Film
description: A survey of all stages of filmmaking in chronological order, from the inception to the release of a film project. Exploration of the ways scripts are developed, productions are planned and executed, visual effects are designed, and distribution deals are secured.

name: Art Direction for Film
description: Introduction to the principles of art direction in film, focusing on crafting visually compelling screen imagery. Exploration of the Art Department’s function and industry-standard practices in shaping the visual world of film, television, and streaming media productions.

name: Film Genres
description: Introduction to the history, theory, and analysis of film genres: drama, comedy, horror, action, fantasy, science fiction, musical, western, crime, and others. Emphasis on the key functions of genre: (i) an industrial category used for marketing purposes, (ii) a system of narrative and audiovisual codes and conventions, and (iii) a contract between filmmaker and audience to deliver a certain emotional experience.

name: The Horror Film
description: A critical and historical survey of the horror film genre, from the silent film era to the present day. Examination of the genre’s philosophical, literary, and artistic progenitors, historical origins and evolution, industrial contexts, core characteristics, major themes, narrative conventions, character designs, uncanny settings, expressionistic aesthetics, stylistic features, disorienting sounds and other affective powers, psychoanalytic interpretations, sub-categories, well-known masters, and cultural significance.

name: The Historical Film
description: A critical survey of the historical film genre. Exploration of theories of historical fiction with an emphasis on cinematic representations of the past.

name: Animation
description: Introduction to the history of animation as an art form, from its pre-cinematic origins to the present day. Exploration of the fundamental characteristics of animated film.

name: Animation II
description: A theoretical inquiry into animation as a dynamic and evolving medium. Exploration of animation’s materiality, its function as a site of performance, and its intermedial relationships.

name: Japanese Animation
description: A comprehensive study of Japanese animation, from its early twentieth-century origins to its development as a global cultural phenomenon. Exploration of anime as both a national and transnational medium through film and media theory, aesthetics, and fan studies.

name: Transmedia Storytelling
description: An intensive study in the history, theory, and practice of transmedia storytelling, from its emergence in the early 2000s to its widespread adoption across contemporary media cultures. Exploration of how narrative content unfolds across multiple platforms – literature, film, television, comics, podcasts, video games, web series, mobile apps, social media, and XR environments – each contributing uniquely to an expansive story world.

name: Cinema and the Graphic Novel
description: A critical and historical study of the aesthetic relationship between cinema and the graphic novel, focusing on their formal, thematic, and narrative convergences. Examination of the interdependence of the two media, particularly in framing, editing, lighting, and modes of visual storytelling.

name: Cinema and Video Games
description: A comparative study of cinema and video games. Exploration of the historical, cultural, aesthetic, narrative, technological, and industrial intersections between cinema and video games through the writings of game designers, film scholars, and media theorists.

name: Special Topics: Screenwriting Everywhere All at Once
description: This course is designed to provide a fresh, inspiring and practical perspective in introducing the art and craft of screenwriting. It is comparative in nature, both regionally and globally.

name: French Civilisation I
description: Enhancement of the written and spoken French through usage of media and literary texts. Observation of French language-based civilization and cultures through available information tools.

name: Modern French Literature I
description: Study of the leading 20th century French innovative poets and writers with special attention to developments in contemporary French literature (Apollinaire; Dada and surrealism: Breton, Eluard, Desnos, etc.; Gide; Proust; Valéry; Prévert). Improvement of written and oral expression in French through presentations and written assignments.

name: French-Turkish/Turkish-French Translation I
description: Techniques of translation from and into French. Translational analysis of texts covering such diverse topics as philosophy, social sciences, translation theory and the EU, with related translation exercises.

name: French-Turkish/Turkish-French Translation II
description: Techniques of translating from and into French. Translational analysis of texts covering such diverse topics as poetry, the story, literary criticsm and art history, with related translation exercises.

name: French Culture I
description: Enhancement of the written and spoken French through broadcast and narrowcast media. Study of French language-based cultures through extant information sources.

name: French Culture II
description: Further enhancement of the language skills and knowledge of French culture through texts and similar material on the French intellectual history.

name: French in Press
description: Study of the basic concepts of print media in the French language. Analysis of the structure of journalistic text.

name: Advanced French Language Skills
description: Advanced French grammar and reading skills. Study of more complex syntactic structures.

name: Elementary German I
description: Introduction to German. Equal emphasis on reading, writing, speaking and listening comprehension, geared to first stage of A1 level of CEFR.

name: Elementary German II
prerequisites: GER 101 or consent of the instructor
description: Continuation of GER 101; geared to second and last stage of A1 level of CEFR.

name: Concentrated Elementary German
description: A concentrated beginner’s course covering levels A.1.1 and A.1.2 of the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages. Initiating and maintaining basic social interactions such as greetings, farewells, and requesting information.

name: Pre-Intermediate German I
prerequisites: GER 102 or consent of the instructor
description: Continuation of GER 102. Detailed approach to German grammar and sentence structure; further emphasis on reading, writing, speaking and listening comprehension; geared to the first stage of A2 level of CEFR.

name: Pre-Intermediate German II
prerequisites: GER 201 or consent of the instructor
description: Continuation of GER 201. Detailed approach to German grammar and sentence structure; further emphasis on reading writing, speaking and listening comprehension; geared to second stage of A2 level of CEFR.

name: Intermediate German I
prerequisites: GER 202 or consent of the instructor
description: Intensive instruction for careful reading of texts and further elaboration of grammatical and syntactical features. Equal emphasis on reading, writing, speaking and listening comprehension; geared to first stage of B1 level of CEFR.

name: Intermediate German II
prerequisites: GER 301 or consent of the instructor
description: Continuation of GER 301; geared to second stage of B1 level of CEFR.

name: Intermediate German III

description: Continuation of GER 302. Reinforcement of grammatical and syntactical features. Equal emphasis on reading, writing, speaking and listening comprehension.

name: Upper-Intermediate German I
prerequisites: GER 403 or consent of the instructor
description: Continuation of GER 403. Reinforcement of grammar and sentence structures with strong emphasis on vocabulary as used in German print media.

name: Upper-Intermediate German II
description: Development of B-2 level language skills, including reading and understanding texts such as literary prose and articles on contemporary issues, expressing ideas and opinions on sophisticated topics in both speaking and writing, and following extended spoken discourse such as lectures, TV documentaries, and news reports. Grammar points covered include indirect speech (Konjunktiv 1), passive voice, nominalization, infinitival clauses and participial phrases.

name: Translation I
description: Translation of texts, selected from various journals, newspapers and works of literature from German into and from Turkish.

name: Translation II
description: Further enchancement of translation of texts on current issues, selected from various magazines, newspapers and works of literature from German into and from Turkish.

name: German Civilization I
description: Overview of the linguistic, political and cultural history of the German-speaking countries from the Germanic peoples to 1933. Literary texts and authentic historical documents to investigate historical and political events.

name: German Civilization II
description: Overview of the linguistic, political and cultural history of German-speaking countries from 1933 to present time. Literary texts and authentic historical documents to investigate historical and political events.

name: Modern German Literature I
description: Reading and discussion of works selected from modern German and Austrian authors.

name: Modern German Literature II
description: Further enchancement of the reading and discussion of works selected from modern German and Austrian authors.
