prerequisites: GER 405 or consent of the instructor
description: Intensive study of a theme, movement, genre or author having special significance in German civilization, culture, literature or linguistics. Topics vary from year to year.

name: Modern Greek for Beginners I
description: Introduction to the Modern Greek language: The Greek alphabet, elementary vocabulary, basic nouns and adjectives, syntax, the three genders, the present tense and the stem of the simple past tense.

name: Modern Greek for Beginners II
prerequisites: GR 101 or consent of the instructor
description: Introducing more vocabulary and training students to hold simple conversations pertaining to everyday life situations. Emphasis on practicing the simple past tense and the tenses formed from its stem.

name: Ancient Greek I
description: Ancient Greek courses at the elementary level are intended for students who wish to learn the basic grammar of the Ancient Greek. Elementary readings from simplified texts of Greek authors are part of the course work.

name: Ancient Greek II
prerequisites: GR 111 or consent of the instructor
description: Ancient Greek courses at the elementary level are intended for students who wish to learn the basic grammar of the Ancient Greek. Elementary readings from simplified texts of Greek authors are part of the course work.

name: Intermediate Modern Greek I
prerequisites: GR 102 or consent of the instructor
description: Gradual introduction of complex vocabulary, intensive oral practice to make the students capable of expressing themselves in more sophisticated issues. Emphasis on conjunctions and the middle-passive verbs.

name: Intermediate Modern Greek II
prerequisites: GR 201 or consent of the instructor
description: Intensive teaching of advanced vocabulary by means of literary and non-literary texts.

name: Ancient Greek III
prerequisites: GR 112 or consent of the instructor
description: Ancient Greek courses at the intermediate level are a continuation of GR 101-102. The courses include further study of irregular verbs, of the subjunctive and the optative, as well as an analysis of various syntactical phenomena.

name: Ancient Greek IV
prerequisites: GR 211 or consent of the instructor
description: Ancient Greek courses at the intermediate level are a continuation of GR 101-102. The courses include further study of irregular verbs, of the subjunctive and the optative, as well as an analysis of various syntactical phenomena.

name: Advanced Modern Greek I
prerequisites: GR 202 or consent of the instructor
description: Enhancing the students' level of reading and listening comprehension skills and training them to produce samples of writing in Greek.

name: Advanced Modern Greek II
prerequisites: GR 301 or consent of the instructor
description: The reading of Greek prose from literature, the press, the internet, and the like. Basic elements of the history of the Modern Greek language and literature, its relation to the Ancient Greek language (kathareuousa vs. demotiki), its main periods and representative authors as well as the Turkish vocabulary which has entered into Modern Greek, with expressions and conceptual constructions common in both Modern Greek and Turkish.

name: Ancient Greek V
prerequisites: GR 212 or consent of the instructor
description: An advanced course in Ancient Greek offering intensive instruction through close reading of prescribed texts. Further elaboration on grammatical and syntactical features when necessary.

name: Ancient Greek VI
prerequisites: GR 311 or consent of the instructor
description: An in-depth study of a prescribed author (of the Classical or the Byzantine period) or an anthology of Greek prose to help students enhance their skills in handling sophisticated texts in Ancient Greek.

name: Historical Method & Thought I
description: An introduction to the discipline of history and its sources. A survey of historiography and of the variety, traditions and analytical tools of historical writing.

name: Historical Method & Thought II
description: An introduction to historiography and to the methods of historical writing through the study of a wide variety of authors, past and present. The aim is to expose the students to a selection of texts that illustrate the evolution of the discipline, the wide range of approaches used in history, and the interdisciplinary nature of research in the humanities and the social sciences.

name: The Making of the Modern World I
description: A comparative inquiry into the origins, development and interaction of world civilizations. Exploration of the ancient, classical, Byzantine, medieval, Islamic and early Renaissance past of the Mediterranean region and the Near East; the impact of the early Turkic peoples in Central Asia and the Islamic World; the diverse cultures of South East Asia, China and Japan.

name: The Making of the Modern World II
description: A comparative exploration of the political, social and economic worlds of the three major Islamic empires of the early modern age; the Renaissance and the Reformation; the making of the absolutist states of Europe; science and commerce; the English Revolution and the Enlightenment; the American, French and Russian Revolutions of the modern age; the Industrial Revolution; nationalism and imperialism; World Wars I and II; the decline and transformation of China, Japan, India, the Ottoman world, Iran and Egypt in the modern age. Weekly discussion sessions and the study of audio- visual materials required.

name: Introduction to Archaeology I
description: Introduction to the field of archaeology, history of archaeology as a discipline in Europe and in Turkey, survey of archaeological methodology and techniques, site formation processes, analysis and interpretation of material culture, absolute and relative dating, interdisciplinary co-operation in archaeological projects.

name: Introduction to the History of Art and Visual Culture
description: Introduction to the historical study of art and visual culture. A selective survey of major trends and significant monuments in world art and architecture.

name: Ancient History & Archaeology of the Near East I
description: Survey of major transformations in the early history of the Ancient Near East from mobile hunter-gatherers to sedentary villagers, large urban centers, and state formation and early empires. Investigation of areas including Anatolia, Iran, Iraq, Syria and Palestine.

name: Ancient History & Archaeology of the Near East II
description: Survey of historical periods in the Ancient Near East within a chronological framework from the end of the third millennium to the fifth century B.C., integration of archaeological evidence with textual information for the historical narrative of the development of the Near East until the impact of Hellenism.

name: History of Medieval Turco-Persian Societies 800-1250
description: History of the geography and peoples of Central Asia, Iran and Anatolia between the ninth and the thirteenth centuries. The encounter and interaction between Turkic and Iranian societies within the wider context of the medieval eastern Islamic World.

name: Ottoman History 1300-1600
description: Survey of Ottoman history between ca. 1300 and ca 1600. The formation and subsequent transformations of the polity; the key issues in Ottoman social, economic and cultural history.

name: Islamic History and Societies,600-1000
description: The formation and transformation of Islamic societies starting with the rise of Islam in Arabia until the eleventh century. The foundations of Islam, the impact of conquest, the context of religious dissent and schism, concepts of leadership, the implications of sectarian divisions, status of non-muslim communities, the challenges faced by the caliphal-imperial order, law and society, reasons of political fragmentation, philosophical and scientific ventures, encounters in art and architecture, expression of Arab and Iranian identities through literature, urban culture, international trade, writing as a cultural value.

name: Islamic History & Societies,1000-1500
description: A survey of Islamic societies from the decline of caliphal-imperial authority to the emergence of the three early modern empires (Safavid, Ottoman and Mugal). The establishment of Turkic dynasties, the expansion of Islam into Anatolia and South Asia, the rise and role of the New Persian Language, the institutionalization of Sufizm, the rise of the madrasa, impact of the crusades, theoretical and applied sciences, Mongol invasions, post-Mongol social and political re-ordering.

name: Ottoman Cultural History
description: Survey of Ottoman cultural history from the early fourteenth to the beginning of the twentieth centuries. Critical readings in changing cultural realities of the Ottoman realm.

name: Western European Societies,politics & Cultures 1450-1750
description: Western European History between ca. 1450 and 1750. Focus on social, economic, cultural and political history.

name: Western European Societies,politics & Cultures 1750-1890
description: European History between 1750 and 1890. The Frech Revolution and its impact, modernizing development of Europe in the nineteenth century.

name: History of the Americas,1750 to the Present
description: Introductory material will deal with constructing a background of what the new world meant for the old in the context of mercantile capitalism. This will be followed by a survey of the interdependent and unequal development of two continents from George Washington to Simon Bolivar: The making of the American Revolution and its global significance.

name: Ottoman History, 1590-1790
description: An overview of Ottoman history from circa 1590 to circa 1790. Focus on the transformation of Ottoman state and society in a comparative and connected perspective around key issues of demographic, environmental, social, political, cultural and economic history.

name: Ottoman History, 1790-1908
description: An overview of the Ottoman Empire from circa 1790 until 1908. Emphasis on the social, political and military networks, the emergence and development of the modern state in the nineteenth century, the Empire's disintegration after World War I.

name: History of Modern Turkey
description: Late Ottoman and Republican history up to the 2000's. Discussion of the Ottoman Legacy and the making of the nation-state, followed by a study of the evolution of the political and social structures during the Republican era in a comparative perspective.

name: Hittite History & Archaeology
description: Survey of material culture and translations of Hittite texts. Political and cultural history, mythology and religion, as well as developments in art and architecture; assessment of Hittite cultural synthesis in an Anatolian context and within the larger framework of the Eastern Mediterranean.

name: Anatolian Iron Age
description: Survey of Anatolian Iron Age cultures from the disintegration of the Hittite Empire to the 6th century B.C. covering the Neo-Hittite city-states, Urartian Kingdom, Phrygia, Lydia and Caria. Topics include cultural continuity, impact of the Assyrian Empire, Phoenician and Greek cultural, and economic interactions with Anatolia.

name: History of the Byzantine Empire,4th-9th Centuries
description: A Survey of the Late Roman and early Byzantine world from the foundation of Constantinople in 330 to the end of iconoclasm in 843. Transformation of the Roman Empire into the Byzantine Empire in the late antique period; the transformation and challenges Byzantine Society faced in the first few centuries of the Middle Ages.

name: History of the Byzantine Empire,9th-15th Centuries
description: A survey of Byzantine history from the struggles and transformations of the 8th and 9th centuries to the Ottoman conquest of Constantinople in 1453. Major political, social, economic and cultural developments, focusing on topics such as social and economic structures, religion as institution and practice and arts.

name: Aegean History & Archaeology I
description: Survey of Aegean Archaeology starting from the Neolithic period to the end of the second millennium, covering mainland Greece, Aegean Islands, Western Anatolia, Crete and Cyprus.

name: Aegean History & Archaeology II
description: Survey of Aegean archaeology and history from the end of the second millennium to the sixth century B.C. The cultural foundations and basis of classical antiquity within the larger Eastern Mediterranean context.

name: History & Archaeology of Ancient Iran I
description: Survey of ancient Iranian archaeology and history starting from the Neolithic period to the end of the third millennium BC, covering prehistoric developments of the region, the Uruk expansion into the Iranian Plateau and the ensuing Proto-Elamite period including its ties to the Central Asian cultures. Topics include regional differentiation, impact of contact with Mesopotamian urban culture, development of urban complexity and commercial ties to cultures in Central Asia and the Indus Valley.

name: History & Archaeology of Ancient Iran II
description: Survey of ancient Iranian archaeology and history from the beginning of the second millennium to the fourth century B.C., covering the Elamite and Neo-Elamite periods until the establishment of the Achaemenid Persian Empire and its encounter with the Hellenized world. Topics include the interaction of successive regional polities with neighboring states and the development of complex economic, political and social structures and institutions within the Eastern Mediterranean framework and extending to the Indus Valley and Afghanistan.

name: Art & Arch.of the Ancient Roman World
description: Archaeological survey of the ancient Romans from the beginnings of the city of Rome in the early Iron Age to Late Antiquity focusing on major developments in Roman material culture, particularly artworks, buildings, and cities. Emphasis on topics ranging from commemorative and decorative art, historical narrative, and political iconography to building types and functions and the specific Etrusco-Roman notion of space, land division, and city planning.

name: Art & Architecture of the Islamic World I
description: A survey of the art and architecture of the Islamic world from the 7th through the 13th centuries. Artistic patronage of various dynasties in the Middle East and the Mediterranean; aesthetical, cultural and political context of the production and use of works of art; cultural encounters with traditions within and outside of the Islamic world.

name: The Art & Architecture of the Middle Ages
description: Medieval art and architecture in the Christian East, Europe and the Islamic world between the 4th and the 14th centuries. Emphasis on the larger cultural, political, and social context of medieval art and architecture; cross-cultural interactions and influences between the Christian and the Islamic worlds.

name: Renaissance,baroque Art & Architecture
description: A survey of trends in European art and architecture between the 14th and the 18th centuries. The role of the major urban centers of southern and northern Europe in shaping the new intellectual position of the artist in society; the meaning of the classical heritage; the role of patronage; the formation of genres; the interaction between centers and peripheries; the evolution of concepts of space in relation to social and scientific developments.

name: History of Modern Art & Architecture
description: A survey of artistic and architectural production from the late eighteenth century to recent trends. The connections between social transformations and the emergence of new paradigms of visual representation and expression; the interaction between regional and global trends, between western and non-western worlds, between tradition and innovation.

name: Historiography I
description: A critical and comparative review of Western and Eastern historiography and literary methods. Special attention will be given to the relationship between the historian and his era.

name: Historiography II
description: A critical and comparative review of Western and Eastern historiography and literary methods. Special attention will be given to the relationship between the historian and his era.

name: History & Urbanism
description: A history of urbanism from ancient to modern times. Survey of available evidence on the emergence of the city, and its transformations through various periods in history up to the emergence of the industrial city.

name: Seminar in Ottoman History II
description: An in-depth study of selected topics in Ottoman history from the rise of the Empire down to the Tanzimat. The course will be organized around readings on selected themes in institutional, social and intellectual history.

name: Ottoman Social & Economic History II
description: Complementing courses on Ottoman history and parallel to courses on European social and economic history, these courses will address the main issues related to economic and social life in the Ottoman Empire, and aspects of change starting with the sixteenth century; special emphasis will be given to the economic organization of the Empire, the role of the state in the economy, the impact of Western economies on the Ottoman economy, and the attempts at modernization/rationalization of the nineteenth century.

name: Chinese History: From Imperial to Modern China I
description: Selected topics in the history of imperial and modern China. The course will emphasize major periods and themes in the political, social, and economic developments as well as the cultural, intellectual, and institutional history of the Chinese world.

name: Chinese History: From Imperial to Modern China II
description: Selected topics in the history of imperial and modern China. The course will emphasize major periods and themes in the political, social, and economic developments as well as the cultural, intellectual, and institutional history of the Chinese world.

name: Japanese History: From Feudal to Modern Japan I
description: Selected topics in the history of feudal and modern Japan. The course will emphasize major periods, topics in the political, social, and economic developments as well as the cultural, intellectual, and institutional history of Japan.

name: Japanese History: From Feudal to Modern Japan II
description: Selected topics in the history of feudal and modern Japan. The course will emphasize major periods, topics in the political, social, and economic developments as well as the cultural, intellectual, and institutional history of Japan.

name: Korean History I
description: Korean history in the periods from the formation of the Three Kingdoms (668 A.D.) to the Early Period of Choson, which is the last dynasty of Korea, until the Japanese Invasions in 1590s. Emphasis on selected topics in the political, social, and economic developments as well as the cultural, intellectual and institutional history of Korean Peninsula.

name: Korean History II
description: Modern history of Korea from the late Choson Period (16th to 19th century), and the Colonial Period (1905-1945) to the Korean War (1950-1953). Emphasis on the political, social, and economic transitions together with the cultural, intellectual, and institutional transformations.

name: Hist.of the Roman Republic & Empire
description: History of the Roman world from the beginnings of the Republic in the 6th century BC to the crisis of the empire in the 3rd century AD. Topics covered include political, social, economic and cultural developments in the Mediterranean basin under the republican and imperial rule of the Romans.

name: Seminar in Byzantine History
description: Detailed investigation of a selected topic in the social, economic, political, or cultural history of the Byzantine Empire, with particular attention to major controversies or disputed questions of historical analysis and interpretation. Students are expected to read relevant primary sources in English translation, explore archaeological and/or artistic evidence if available, and evaluate critically the secondary literature on the chosen topic.

name: Seminar in Ottoman Sources
description: A selected reading of Ottoman sources in English and Turkish. Each selection will be studied for what it reveals about Ottoman culture, society and institutions.

name: Histories of Medicine
description: An elective course exploring Histories of Medicine.

name: Early Modern Istanbul: Urbanity, Architecture, Representation
description: An elective course exploring Early Modern Istanbul: Urbanity, Architecture, Representation.

name: Cultural History of Iran I
description: An in-depth interdisciplinary introduction to the cultural history of the greater Iranian world from Mesopotamia to Central Asia from Late Antiquity (5th - 7th c.) to the coming of the Mongols (13th c.). A survey of the political and social history; study of such major themes as kingship and court culture, Islamization, linguistic heritage, literary revival, poetry, socio-religious institutions, trade and exchange, architecture, and the arts (ceramics, metalwork, painting).

name: Islam in Medieval and Early Modern Iberia
description: An elective course exploring Islam in Medieval and Early Modern Iberia.

name: History of Science and Technology in Islamic Societies
description: An elective course exploring History of Science and Technology in Islamic Societies.

name: Special Topics: Late Ottoman & Early Republican Memoirs as a Historical Source
description: A survey of the consolidation of the Balkan nation-states and the projects of political and cultural modernization, launched by their political elites. Chronological coverage of the period between the Berlin Treaty (1878) and the end of WWI (1918).

name: Special Topics: Culture as a Topic of Hist.inquiry
description: An advanced special topics course examining Culture as a Topic of Hist.inquiry.

name: Special Topics: History of Science & Technology in Islamic Societies
description: An advanced special topics course examining History of Science & Technology in Islamic Societies.

name: Special Topics: Ottoman History,1590-1790
description: Study of selected topics in history not covered in other courses at undergraduate level.

name: Special Topics: Otoman Ist.: Arch,urban.represen.
description: Study of selected topics in history not covered in other courses at undergraduate level.

name: Special Topics: In Digital History
description: An advanced special topics course examining In Digital History.

name: Special Topics: History of Science & Technology in Islamic Societies
description: An advanced special topics course examining History of Science & Technology in Islamic Societies.

name: Special Topics: Histories of Medicine
description: An advanced special topics course examining Histories of Medicine.

name: Special Topics: Early Modern Istanbul: Urbanity, Architecture,representation
description: An advanced special topics course examining Early Modern Istanbul: Urbanity, Architecture,representation.

name: Special Topics: Islamic Legal History
description: An advanced special topics course examining Islamic Legal History.

name: Special Topics: France 1661-1789
description: Study of selected topics in history not covered in other courses at undergraduate level.

name: Special Topics: In History: The Archaeology of the Roman Economy
description: An advanced special topics course examining In History: The Archaeology of the Roman Economy.

name: Special Topics: Major Themes in Global History
description: The purpose of this seminar is two-fold: first, to cultivate an understanding of political, economic, social, and cultural forces in shaping history from a world historical perspective; and second, to confront the study of global history as a conceptual problem. To achieve these goals, we will develop a historical trajectory that will conceive global history in its totality structured by the interaction of different geographical zones, examine major theoretical problems, and read exemplary studies that highlight certain characteristic themes in the study of global history.

name: Special Topics: Technology & Media in the Late Ottoman Empire & Egypt
description: An advanced special topics course examining Technology & Media in the Late Ottoman Empire & Egypt.

name: Special Topics: World Environmental History
description: An advanced special topics course examining World Environmental History.

name: Special Topics: HIST Special Topics Virgil
description: An advanced special topics course examining HIST Special Topics Virgil.

name: Special Topics: Islam Medieval and Early Modern Iberia
description: An advanced special topics course examining Islam Medieval and Early Modern Iberia.

description: Study of selected topics in history not covered in other courses at undergraduate level.

description: Study of selected topics in history not covered in other courses at undergraduate level.

name: Special Topics: East European Post Soviet History
description: Study of selected topics in history not covered in other courses at undergraduate level.

name: Special Topics: Knowledge and Education in Islamicate Societies
description: An advanced special topics course examining Knowledge and Education in Islamicate Societies.

name: Special Topics: A Global History of Capitalism
description: Study of selected topics in history not covered in other courses at undergraduate level.

name: Special Topics: Migration and Human Mobility in the Late Ottoman
description: An advanced special topics course examining Migration and Human Mobility in the Late Ottoman.

name: Special Topics: A Global History of Capitalism II
description: Study of selected topics in history not covered in other courses at undergraduate level.

name: Cultural Encounters I
description: An interdisciplinary humanities survey, designed to introduce students to cultures east and west, ancient and modern which have, over time, impacted and interacted with their own culture, and thus to encourage critical reflection on this wider cultural heritage with emphasis on philosophy, literature, arts, political thought, science and religion. Readings in primary and secondary materials to analyze, compare and contrast ideas, paradigms, world views in ancient, classical and medieval civilizations.

name: Cultural Encounters II
description: An interdisciplinary humanities survey, designed to introduce students to cultures east and west, ancient and modern which have, over time, impacted and interacted with their own culture, and thus to encourage critical reflection on this wider cultural heritage with emphasis on philosophy, literature, arts, political thought, science and religion. Readings in primary and secondary materials from the Renaissance era to the present to analyze, compare and contrast ideas, paradigms, world views.

name: Elementary Hungarian I
description: Introduction to Hungarian language and culture. Equal emphasis on reading, writing, speaking and listening comprehension.

name: Elementary Hungarian II
prerequisites: HUNG 101 or consent of the instructor
description: Continuation of HUNG 101; geared to second and last stage of A1 level of Common European Framework of Reference for Languages.

name: Pre-Intermediate Hungarian I
prerequisites: HUNG 102 or consent of the instructor
description: Continuation of HUNG 102. Detailed approach to Hungarian grammar and culture; further emphasis on reading, writing, speaking and listening comprehension; geared to the first stage of A2 level of Common European Framework of Reference for Languages.

name: Pre-Intermediate Hungarian II
prerequisites: HUNG 201 or consent of the instructor
description: Continuation of HUNG 201. Detailed approach to Hungarian grammar and culture; further emphasis on reading, writing, speaking and listening comprehension; geared to second stage of A2 level of Common European Framework of Reference for Languages.

name: Intermediate Hungarian I
prerequisites: HUNG 202 or consent of the instructor
description: Intensive instruction for careful reading of texts and further elaboration of grammatical and textual features. Further knowledge about Hungarian culture, geography and customs.

name: Intermediate Hungarian II
prerequisites: HUNG 301 or consent of the instructor
description: Consolidation of intermediate grammar and vocabulary; fluency in conversational skills. Reinforcement of communicative skills (reading, writing, speaking and listening) and development of further language functions related to themes both in the Hungarian and Turkish culture.

name: Intermediate Hungarian III
prerequisites: HUNG 302 or consent of the instructor
description: Continuation of HUNG 302. Reinforcement of grammatical and syntactical features.

name: Upper-Intermediate Hungarian I
prerequisites: HUNG 303 or consent of the instructor
description: Continuation of HUNG 303. Reinforcement of grammar and word order with strong emphasis on vocabulary as used in Hungarian media.

name: Upper-Intermediate Hungarian II
prerequisites: HUNG 401 or consent of the instructor
description: Development of B2 level language skills, including reading and understanding texts such as literary prose and articles on contemporary issues; expressing ideas and opinions on complex topics in both speaking and writing, and following extended spoken discourse such as lectures, TV documentaries and news reports.

name: Translation I
prerequisites: HUNG 401 or consent of the instructor
description: Translation of texts, selected from various journals, newspapers and works of literature from Hungarian into Turkish and from Turkish to Hungarian.

name: Translation II
prerequisites: HUNG 401 or consent of the instructor
description: Further enhancement of translation of texts on current issues, selected from various magazines, newspapers and works of literature from Hungarian into and from Turkish.

name: Hungarian Civilization I
prerequisites: HUNG 401 or consent of the instructor
description: Overview of the linguistic, political and cultural history of Hungary to 1849. Literary texts and authentic historical documents investigating historical and political events.

name: Hungarian Civilization II
prerequisites: HUNG 401 or consent of the instructor
description: Overview of the linguistic, political and cultural history of Hungary from 1849. Literary texts and authentic historical documents investigating historical and political events.

name: Modern Hungarian Literature I
prerequisites: HUNG 401 or consent of the instructor
description: Reading and discussion of works selected from Hungarian authors in the 19-20th century.

name: Modern Hungarian Literature II
prerequisites: HUNG 401 or consent of the instructor
description: Further enhancement of the reading and discussion of works selected from Hungarian authors in the 20th century and from contemporary authors.

name: Economic History of Europe
description: Life and the economy before the Industrial Revolution: the rise and fall of the manorial system, the prudent peasant and open fields, the growth of labor productivity in early modern English agriculture, the efficiency and distributional consequences of eighteenth century enclosures. The Industrial Revolution; demand vs. supply, the demographic transition, life in France and England, the standard of living debate and consumption.

name: Special Topics: Cross Culturel Issues in Business
description: The course aims to incorporate the latest important research and contemporary insights that have changed the context and environment for international management. It stresses environment, culture, strategy, and the interactions among them.

name: Special Topics: Economic History of Asia
description: East Asia’s economic history offers a lens for understanding how states, markets, and societies transform across time. This course examines the long-run development of Japan, South Korea, China, and Taiwan, tracing how institutions, industrial policy, trade and finance, technology, demography, and international integration shaped growth and distribution.

name: Elementary Italian I
description: Introduction to basic aspects of the Italian grammar. Preparing students to deal competently with a wide range of day-to-day situations in spoken Italian and develop oral skills in simulated contexts.

name: Elementary Italian II
prerequisites: ITA 101 or consent of the instructor
description: Focus on selected aspects of the Italian grammar. Emphasis on listening and reading comprehension.

name: Pre-Intermediate Italian I
prerequisites: ITA 102 or consent of the instructor
description: Review of the main grammatical aspects of A1 level. Consolidating and improving students’ previous knowledge of key basic vocabulary.

name: Pre-Intermediate Italian II
prerequisites: ITA 201 or consent of the instructor
description: Equal emphasis on reading, writing, speaking and listening comprehension. Communicative functions covered: describing places, people and habits in the past; giving a descriptive background of the past; asking and describing physical appearance and character of people in the present and past; talking about schools and the school system; talking about future projects; asking and giving information about renting an apartment; expressing and describing symptoms; asking and replying about physical conditions and health problems.

name: Upper Intermediate Italian I
prerequisites: ITA 202 or consent of the instructor
description: Review of the important grammatical aspects of A2 level. Consolidating and improving students’ previous knowledge of key vocabulary.

name: Upper Intermediate Italian II
prerequisites: ITA 301 or consent of the instructor
description: Equal emphasis on reading, writing, speaking and listening comprehension. Communicative functions covered: talking about social medias and their influence on leisure time; describing and summarizing shows, theatre plays and movies; talking about different kinds of job, expressing opinions about the job situation of one’s country; getting ready for a job interview and writing an e-mail of self-presentation; asking for help, complaining, explaining personal reasons; writing a complaint letter.

name: Advanced Italian I
prerequisites: ITA 302 or consent of the instructor
description: Review of the main grammatical aspects of B1 level. Analysis of advanced grammar and vocabulary.

name: Advanced Italian II
prerequisites: ITA 401 or consent of the instructor
description: Analysis of advanced grammar and vocabulary. Focus on neo-standard variety of Italian language and regionalisms.

name: Italian Civilization I
prerequisites: ITA 402 or consent of the instructor
description: Overview of the economical and cultural changes undertaken in Italy during the 1950s, 1960s and 1970s through authentic material, literary texts and selected movies. Enhancement of written and spoken Italian through selected texts, TV broadcasts and audiovisual material.

name: Italian Civilization II
prerequisites: ITA 402 or consent of the instructor
description: Overview of the political, economical and cultural changes undertaken in Italy from the beginning of the 1980’s to present time. Emphasis on written and spoken Italian through literary texts, audiovisual material, TV programmes and authentic documents.

name: Modern Italian Literature I
prerequisites: ITA 402 or consent of the instructor
description: A general overview of the 20th century Italian Literature Schools. Reading and comprehension of selected works of leading 20th century Italian writers.

name: Modern Italian Literature II
prerequisites: ITA 402 or consent of the instructor
description: Reading and comprehension of selected works of leading 20th and 21st century Italian writers. Geared to second stage of B2 level of Common European Framework of Reference for Languages.

name: Beginners Japanese I
description: Equip the students with conversation, reading, writing, and comprehension skills in Japanese. Basic Japanese grammatical forms, daily conversation, with emphasis on the Hiragana writing system.

name: Beginners Japanese II
description: Focus on the Progressive Tense (Te-form), dictionary forms of verbs, adjectives and comparatives-superlatives in Japanese. Introduction to the Katakana writing system and 100 Kanji (ideograms).

name: Intermediate Japanese I
prerequisites: JP 101 and 102 or consent of the instructor
description: Complex sentence structures; if-clauses, time expressions (sentences with when), and plain versus polite style Japanese. Reading and writing 100 new Kanji.

name: Intermediate Japanese II
prerequisites: JP 201 or the consent of instructor
description: Focus on complex sentence structures. Introduction to active and passive voices, expressions of benefactive acts (giving and receiving acts).

name: Upper Intermediate Japanese I
description: More advanced grammar forms and their usages. Japanese expressions; conversations and reading material in Japanese.

name: Upper Intermediate Japanese II
description: Humble Form and Honorific Form (KEIGO). Practice in conversation and reading material.

name: Advanced Japanese I
description: Advanced level conversations and reading materials dealing with topics in social sciences. Introduction of 80 new reading Kanji and 100 new writing Kanji.

name: Advanced Japanese II
description: Advanced Japanese at a deeper level. Advances level conversations and reading materials dealing with topics in natural sciences and technical subjects.

name: Japanese-Turkish Translation I
description: Techniques of translation from Japanese literature into Turkish. Translating and providing translational analysis of different literary texts such as poetry, short story, literary criticsm from contemporary Japanese authors.

name: Japanese-Turkish Translation II
description: Techniques of translation of texts from diverse areas from Japanese into Turkish. Translational analysis of texts covering various fields such as economy, politics, art and translation theory with related translation exercises.

name: Classical Japanese
description: An introduction to Classical Japanese for students who have completed their formal study of modern standard Japanese. Lectures and exercises on the phonology and grammar of Early Middle Japanese of the Heian period.

name: Beginners Korean I
description: Practice and mastery of Hangul, the Korean alphabet. Acquisition of basic Korean sentential patterns and sound system.

name: Beginners Korean II
prerequisites: KR 101 or consent of the instructor
description: Introduction of a full range of the fundamentals of the Korean language such as an irregular predicates, past and future tenses, honorific and deferential speech styles. 15 further grammar items and 600 new expressions.

name: Intermediate Korean I
prerequisites: KR 102 or consent of the instructor
description: Exploration of grammatically complex structures and communicative situations. More irregular predicates, connectives, sentential transformations, and speech styles such as imperative. 20 further grammar items and 600 new expressions.

name: Intermediate Korean II
prerequisites: KR 201 or consent of the instructor
description: Emphasis on developing further skills in speaking, listening, reading, and writing intermediate level Korean. Introduction to aspects of Korean culture and daily life.

name: Advanced Korean I
prerequisites: KR 202 or consent of the instructor
description: High-intermediate level oral practices and writing exercises. 40 new complex grammar points and 600 new expressions. Learning to communicate in social situations such as daily activities, interests and personal preferences, as well as food, shopping, and lodging; and to ask a variety of questions on directions, prices, and services.

name: Advanced Korean II
prerequisites: KR 301 or consent of the instructor
description: High-intermediate level speaking and writing exercises. Exchange of basic information related to work, school, recreation, particular interests and areas of competence.

name: Advanced Korean III
prerequisites: KR 302 or consent of the instructor
description: Advanced Korean grammar. Reading, writing and speaking on Korean culture, history, customs, folklore and geography.

name: Advanced Korean IV
prerequisites: KR 401 or consent of the instructor
description: Advanced reading, writing and speaking. Participation in most informal and some formal exchanges on a variety of concrete topics relating to events of current, public, and personal interest or individual relevance.

name: Kurdish for Beginners I
description: Basic vocabulary and sentence structures in the present tense in the Kurmanci dialect. Following basic classroom instructions and using key phrases for classroom interaction.

name: Kurdish for Beginners II
description: Basic sentence structures for expressing the present, past, and future. Asking and answering simple questions about immediate needs and everyday topics.

name: Elementary Latin I
description: Introduction to basic Latin syntax, grammar and preliminary vocabulary, with reading of brief passages from Latin authors.

name: Elementary Latin II
prerequisites: LAT 111 or consent of the instructor
description: A continuation of LAT 111; completion of basic grammar with increased facility in reading through selected passages of Latin poetry and prose.

name: Intermediate Latin I
prerequisites: LAT 112 or consent of the instructor
description: Consolidation of the Latin forms and syntax. Emphasis on reading comprehension through the translation of unadapted excerpts from various Latin texts.

name: Intermediate Latin II
prerequisites: LAT 211 or consent of the instructor
description: Reinforcement of grammar. Focus on translation skills through the study of a large sample of classical and medieval Latin texts and the cursory reading of an unabridged work in Latin.

name: Advanced Latin I
prerequisites: LAT 212 or consent of the instructor
description: Enhancing of the translation skills and further reinforcement of grammar. Special emphasis on the historical and literary contexts of the texts studied.

name: Advanced Latin II
prerequisites: LAT 311 or consent of the instructor
description: Translating complex texts with continued emphasis upon the cultural context of these works. An introduction to epigraphy and Church Latin to enhance translation skills acquired previously.

name: Introduction to Law
description: Fundamental concepts; the relationship of law with political phenomena; the features of legal rules; the law and the sovereign relationship; branches of law; different legal systems; Turkish legal system and courts, interpretation methods; introduction to legal methodology.

name: Legal Methodology
description: Legal theories and schools, interpretation methods; the concept of analogy; the concept of legal gaps; academic writing; referencing and academic presentation; determining research topic and the problem, research plan; resources in legal research; doctrinal approach, comparative approach; historical approach; philosophical approach; socio-legal approach; general information on quantitative methods; general information on qualitative methods; the relationship among method, argument and plan.

name: General Principles of Constitutional Law
description: The historical context and evolution of constitutional principles; methods of constitutional interpretation and analysis; basic doctrines concerning the structure of government and the protection of individual rights, sources of constitutional law; types of constitution; the constituent power; sovereignty theories; different types of State organisations; the political power and theories of legitimacy; governmental systems; democracy; electoral systems and political parties; separation of powers; the legislative, executive, and judicial branches; fundamental rights and freedoms; constitutional jurisdiction.

name: Public International Law
description: The subject and structure of public international law; the sources of international law; the law of treaties; the subjects of international law; statehood, recognition, self-determination; international organisations; international law – national law relationship; state jurisdiction in international law; state immunity; diplomatic immunities; international law of the sea; international law of responsibility; use of force in international law.

name: Human Rights Law
description: Fundamental concepts; historical analysis; theories on the sources of rights; the legitimacy of the State from a human rights perspective; individual-state relationship; right holders and duty bearers; the principles of human rights law; the classification of the rights; international human rights law system; the system of United Nations; regional systems; national protection of human rights; the supervision mechanisms of human rights; contemporary issues in human rights law.

name: Legal History
description: The relationship between law and history; Roman law: introduction to the Roman history and Roman law; the sources and fundamental principles of Roman law, Roman personality law, Roman obligation law (from the archaic period until the birth of modern law in Europe); Pre-Islamic Turkish law; Post-Islamic Turkish law; Ottoman law: introduction to Ottoman law, Ottoman personality law, Ottoman family law; Ottoman property law, Ottoman criminal law, Ottoman law after Reforms.

name: Legal Philosophy
description: Fundamental concepts; philosophical background of the legal institutions; natural law / positive law distinction; the legal philosophy in the Ancient age; the philosophy of the religion-based legal systems; the legal philosophy in the Renaissance and ongoing period; modern approaches.

name: Law and Public Policy
description: The concept and ethical value of public policy; stages of the policy cycle model; fundamental concepts of public policy; public policy innovations; behavioural mechanisms and public policy design; constitutional limits of behavioural public policy design; participatory decision-making in public policy; the role of regulatory agencies in public policymaking; transparency in public policy, participation in public policy delivery; data in public policy, open data platforms and policies; artificial intelligence in public policy; social and environmental public policy; the organisational, technical, and legal barriers to policy innovation.

name: International Environmental Law
description: Foundations of international environmental law. Sources of international environmental law.

name: Law and Economics
description: Introduction to law and economics; purpose of law and social welfare theory; why and when do we need law?; concepts of economic efficiency and externality; processes of formation of law; relationship between liberal economy and regulation; regulation methods; economic analysis of property; economic analysis of tort; economic analysis of contract law; economic analysis of family law; economic analysis of criminal law; economic analysis of legal processes; economic analysis of contemporary legal problems.

name: Introduction to Language & Linguistics I
description: An introductory course to the study of language focusing on the properties of natural languages and aiming to familiarize the student with linguistic terminology and the concepts underlying these terms.

name: Introduction to Language & Linguistics II
description: Extension of basic linguistic concepts both in depth and breadth. Practical application to data from a variety of languages with the aim of improving the student's ability to do linguistic analysis.

name: Semantics
description: Study of fundamental elements of semantic theory: compositionality, predication, truth-conditions, quantification, lexical semantics. Discussion of semantic concepts, such as reference, definiteness, negation, modality.

name: Language Contact
description: Multilingualism in societies and the mechanisms of the resultant contact-induced language change. Contact languages such as pidgins, creoles and mixed languages.

name: Discourse as Social Interaction
description: Study of discourse as a social, cultural and practical phenomenon. Discussion of the interaction among discourse, context, power, and ideology.

name: Special Topics: Mathematics and Philosophy in Linguistics
description: Mathematics of linguistic description and grammar. Computational infrastructure of linguistic description.

name: Special Topics: Exploring Natural Languages by Modeling
description: Basic concepts of natural grammar. Basic concepts of modeling. Relating natural grammars to computation.

name: Special Topics: Language and Cognition
description: The major objective of this course is to provide an overview of research pertaining to language and its relation to cognition/ mind and brain. The first six weeks will be oriented towards a discussion of the knowledge of language; evolutionary bases of language; how nature and nurture both serve as driving forces for its emergence.

name: Special Topics: Corpus Linguistics and Pragmatics
description: An advanced special topics course examining Corpus Linguistics and Pragmatics.

name: Creative Writing I
description: The aim of the course is to help the student develop a personal prose style through intensive study of the craft of writing. The focal point is original writing by students, while selected short readings may be also assigned for class discussion.

name: Special Topics: Creative Writing: From Scratch to Masterpiece
description: This is a unique course designed to guide the student into the world of screenwriting while exploring and challenging the universe of literature. The course shares principles with our other classes while maintaining a clearly distinct goal and curriculum.

name: Special Topics: Mythic Struc. & Storytelling in Cinema
description: This course explores the significance of myth for the human psyche and examines the fundamental principles of mythological structures in storytelling, illustrated through examples from world cinema. Students will engage with both traditional and modern narratives by reading, viewing, and analyzing a wide range of sources—including legends, folktales, epics, and urban myths—with a particular emphasis on Turkish mythic traditions.

name: Special Topics: Imagining the Human: Man, Monster, Machine in Literature and Film
description: This course aims to critically engage students with the idea of the anthropocene, tracing literary and film representations of what ‘human’ has meant through the ages and explore what it may mean in the future. These representations will be accompanied by theoretical readings on the human condition.

name: Special Topics: Graphic Novel
description: This course is of interest to anyone concerned with verbal & visual communications, popular forms, mass culture, history, representation, colonialism/post-colonialism, politics, journalism, writing, philosophy, religion, mythology, mysticism, metaphysics, cultural exchanges, aesthetics, modernism/post-modernism, theatre, film, television, streaming, games, comic art, collections, popular art & culture, literature, fine arts, etc.

name: Step II
description: "Power step", a dynamic exercise program. How to "power the moves", by developing new combinations and patterns.

name: Fitness I
description: Techniques of working with weights, achieving of general and maximum strength and endurance. The use of both own body weight and additional weights in completing a series of exercises, consisting of thirty different stations, geared to gain physical and psychological strength and endurance.

name: Fitness II
description: The principles of station and circuit trainings and trainings for acquisition of special strength and endurance for specific branches of sports.

name: Canoe I
description: Practical experience and fundamentals of canoeing. Different boat types such as open canoe, closed canoe and kayak, paddle strokes for each boat type.

name: Canoe II
description: Intermediate canoeing techniques and practice in different boat types such as open canoe, closed canoe and kayak.

name: Yoga and Relaxation Techniques I
description: Principles of KARMA yoga for relaxation techniques and development of the respiration system.

name: Yoga and Relaxation Techniques II
description: Mediation by using RAJA yoga.

name: Health and Sports Clinique I
description: Basic principles of cardiovascular endurance, weight control, strength, flexibility, first aid, and nutrition. Performance tests.

name: Health and Sports Clinique II
description: Techniques for cardiovascular endurance, weight control, strength flexibility and nutrition. Advanced performance tests.

name: Aerobic I
description: General principles of low impact exercises, including non-ballistic aerobic movements which minimize joint stress. Added light hand held weight work to develop strength.

name: Aerobic II
description: Aerobic exercises like march, kick and hop. General principles of low ad high impact exercises. A mixture of ballistic and non-ballistic movements to give a safe challenging workout and to develop fluidity of motion and cardiovascular strength.

name: Aerobic Dance I
description: A dynamic and rhythmic exercise class, combining basic dance and aerobic movements to teach funky, hip-hop, salsa, cha-cha and similar dance techniques. Rhythmic movements, low impact.

name: Aerobic Dance II
description: Modern moves to classical groove. A high impact class, which incorporates the movement awareness of modern dance.

name: Track and Field I
description: Fundamentals of track and field. Speed and endurance exercises.

name: Track and Field II
description: Techniques of track and field. Special exercises for various branches.

name: Badminton I
description: Fundamentals and practice of basic badminton techniques: wrists works and forehand, backhand, drop and smash techniques.

name: Badminton II
description: Techniques like forehand, backhand, drop smash applied in singles, doubles and mixed doubles games.

name: Basketball I
description: Training in fundamentals of basketball. Introduction to offensive and defensive moves in 2 on 2 and 3 on 3 settings.

name: Basketball II
description: Advanced techniques of basketball. Introduction to team offensive and defense systems.

name: Soccer I
description: Fundamental rules and practice of basic soccer techniques: dribbling, passing, stopping and shooting.

name: Soccer II
description: Advanced techniques of soccer and systems: (4-4-2), (3-5-2), (3-4-3). Introduction to team and defense systems.

name: Tennis I
description: Fundamentals and practice of basic tennis techniques: forehand, backhand and the combination of those two strikes.

name: Tennis II
description: Advanced techniques of tennis: ground strokes, servers, volleys, and game strategies.

name: Volleyball I
description: Fundamental rules and practice of basic volleyball techniques: block, underhand pass, over-arm, pass and serve.

name: Volleyball II
description: Advanced techniques of volleyball. Introduction to team offense and defense systems.

name: Wrestling I
description: Fundamental rules of wrestling and practice of basic wrestling techniques: arm-drag, cross-buttock, lifting holds.

name: Wrestling II
description: Techniques of Free and Greco-Roman wrestling and defensive and strategic wrestling techniques.

name: Self Defense Sports I
description: The basics of Teak-wan-do and Aikido self-defense techniques. Teak-wan-do: hand and foot techniques like Palhagi and Chirigi and defense and counter attack positions.

name: Self Defense Sports II
description: Combinations of Teak-wan-do techniques; combinations of Aikido techniques.

name: Sports for the Handicapped I
description: Physical exercises designed for the handicapped to improve their psychological and physical strengths.

name: Sports for the Handicapped II
description: Specially designed sport games for groups with various types of handicap, with special rules, and competition.

name: Rock Climbing I
description: Introduction to rock-climbing at the climbing wall which includes overhangs, cracks and bulges. Basic ascending and descending techniques.

name: Rock Climbing II
description: Advanced rock-climbing techniques. Soloing and team work at the climbing. Advanced use of climbing equipment.

name: Rowing I
description: Fundamentals of sculling and sweep rowing techniques Exercises in the rowing pool.

name: Rowing II
description: Intermediate rowing techniques and basic principles of boat rigging. Exercises on the lake.

name: Latin-Aero Dance I
description: Fundamentals and practice of basic international Latin dance techniques: Poise, footwork, hip movements, bounces, rhythmic interpretations. Preparation of body for Latin dance techniques through aerobics and stretching exercises.

name: Latin-Aero Dance II
description: Advanced techniques of Latin dancing. Developing fluidity of motion and cardiovascular strength with different combinations of Latin dance steps.

name: Sailing
description: Wind, navigation and basic sailing information. On board practices, theoretical and practical instruction on windsurfing techniques.

name: Table Tennis
description: Fundamentals and practice of table tennis techniques: forehand, backhand, topspin, backspin, serves, and game strategies.

name: Elementary Swimming
description: Basic principles of swimming techniques: ability to float, breath holding, elementary backstroke, front crawl, sidestroke and aquatic safety skills.

name: Advanced Swimming
description: General and advanced principles of swimming: refinement of strokes (front, back crawl, elementary backstroke), introduction to breaststroke, turns and survival skills.

name: Introduction to Chess
description: Fundamental rules of chess, functions and usage of chess; the functions and usage of chess pieces in the development of the game.

name: Advanced Chess
description: Advanced chess analysis, the main ideas for openings, mid-game logic, and training in end games.

name: Futsal I
description: Fundamental rules and drills of futsal techniques: dribbling, passing, shooting and stopping.

name: Futsal II
description: Practice of advanced futsal techniques: (2-2), (3-1), (1-2-1). Introduction to different offensive and defensive strategies.

name: Bridge
description: Introduction to bridge and card playing. Introduction to bidding, openings and their responses.

name: African Dance
description: Fundamentals and practice of African dance techniques: Poise, footwork, polyrhythm, polycentric movements of torso/hip/arm/shoulder/head. Introduction to dances, music, and culture of West Africa. Warming-up exercises, Developing the sense of rhythm.

name: Pilates I
description: Basic techniques for improving flexibility and stability of the torso-stabilizing muscles of the abdomen and lower back using special apparatus. Breathing techniques.

name: Pilates II
description: Advanced techniques for improving flexibility and stability of the torso-stabilizing muscles of the abdomen and lower back using special apparatus. Breathing techniques.

name: Circuit Training I
description: Basic training using body weight or weight equipment in ordered stations with timed rests, targeting acquisition of strength, speed and endurance.

name: Circuit Training II
description: Advanced training using body weight or weight equipment in ordered stations with timed rests, targeting acquisition of strength, speed and endurance.

name: Total-Body Shaping I
description: Basic techniques and exercises accompanied by high tempo music for improving all muscle groups and cardiovascular system.

name: Total-Body Shaping II
description: Advanced techniques and exercises accompanied by high tempo music for improving all muscle groups and cardiovascular system.

name: Basketball Coaching I
description: Theory and application of basketball coaching. Teaching offensive and defensive fundamentals.

name: Basketball Coaching II
description: Theory and application of advanced basketball coaching. Teaching offensive and defensive systems.

name: Soccer Coaching I
description: Theory and techniques in soccer coaching, including offensive and defensive strategies.

name: Soccer Coaching II
description: Advanced techniques in soccer coaching, including offensive and defensive strategies.

name: Skiing I
description: Alpine style skiing theory. Stages of slalom and giant slalom. Basic positions.

name: Skiing II
description: Alpine style skiing. Basic turns. Exercises for parallel turns (christen, short jump, slope turn, slide).

name: Archery
description: Fundamentals and practice of archery techniques: stance, draw, anchor, aim, release, and follow-through. Training includes proper use of equipment, development of concentration, balance, and coordination, as well as safety principles in archery practice.

name: Handball
description: Fundamental rules and practice of basic handball techniques, including passing, catching, dribbling, shooting, and movement with and without the ball. Introduction to basic offensive and defensive principles through small-sided games.

name: Special Topics
description: Semester-specific content addressing various aspects of sports sciences and physical education. Technical and tactical practices of a particular sport, the relationship between exercise and health, sports psychology, training science, motor skills, sports management, or current sports policies.

name: Persian I
description: The alphabet, word structure, phology and morphology of Persian. An applied study on selected texts from classical and modern Persian works.

name: Persian II
description: Word groups, word types and sentence structure (syntax) of Persian. An applied study on selected texts from classical and modern Persian works.

name: Persian III
prerequisites: PER 202 or Consent of the instructor
description: Classical forms and usages in Persian. Selected readings in medieval and early modern texts.

name: Persian IV
prerequisites: PER 203 or Consent of the instructor
description: Forms, themes and tropes in classical Persian poetry, including panegyric, epic and didactic mysticism. Parallels with Ottoman poetry.

name: Introduction to Education
description: The aim of this course is to introduce various aspects of education, teaching, learning, teaching profession, school and education system. The main topics to be covered are: Basic concepts of education, teaching and learning; aims and functions of education; the relationship of education with other fields and sciences; legal, social, cultural, historical, political, economic, philosophical, ethical and psychological foundations of education; methods in educational sciences; school and classroom as an educational and learning environment; teaching as a profession and ethics for teaching profession; current developments in teacher training; key trends in school and education in the twenty-first century.

name: Educational Psychology
description: The aim of this course is to recognize the effects of psychology on the field of education, the psychological dimensions of the learner and learning based on the basic concepts and subjects of psychology. The main topics are: Basic concepts of psychology and educational psychology; research methods in educational psychology; development theories, areas of development and development processes; individual differences in development; basic concepts of learning; factors affecting learning; learning theories; motivation in the learning process.

name: Introduction to Philosophy
description: Survey of the main concepts, problems and approaches in philosophy. An introduction to the techniques of philosophical analysis.

name: Informal Logic
description: Topics of informal logic: Logical consequence, argument patterns, general criteria for good argument, fallacies, and philosophical analysis of argumentative texts.

name: Philosophical Texts
description: Selections from philosophical literature. The method and practice of analyzing philosophical texts.

name: Introduction to Ancient & Medieval Philosophy
description: The evolution of philosophy from its beginning in ancient Greece till the end of the medieval period.

name: Introduction to Modern Philosophy
description: The evolution of modern philosophy from Descartes up to the present.

name: Logic I
description: Propositional logic and first-order monadic quantifier calculus.

name: Logic II
description: First-order quantifier calculus with identity and topics in metalogic.

name: History of Philosophy I
description: A survey of Western philosophy from the pre-Socratic philosophers to Aristotle.

name: History of Philosophy II
description: Study of the relationship of Jewish, Christian and Islamic philosophy to Greek philosophy and scholastic thought systems. Study of writings by Augustine, Thomas Aquinas, Scotus, Ockham and Hellenistic, Roman, Arabic and other medieval philosophers.

name: Philosophy of Science
description: Examination of the goals of science. Scientific explanation, theory construction, the use of models, confirmation of hypotheses, and the status of theoretical entities all discussed within the context of examples from the history of science.

name: Applied Ethics
description: Philosophical analysis of contemporary moral issues, such as abortion, euthanasia, affirmative action, the ethics of charity, animal rights, moral justification of war.

name: Epistemology
description: An examination of philosophical problems encountered in the analysis of the concept of knowledge with respect to the origins, limits and validity of human knowledge.

name: History of Philosophy III
description: A survey of western philosophy from Descartes to Kant. Study of writings by Descartes, Locke, Leibniz, Hume, Kant, Hobbes, Berkeley, Spinoza and Rousseau.

name: History of Philosophy IV
description: A survey of western philosophy from Kant onward. Study of writings by philosophers such as Hegel, Mill, Nietzsche, and Heidegger.

name: Advanced Logic I
description: ZF axioms for set theory, axiom of choice, well ordering, ordinal numbers, cardinal numbers, GCH, ultraproducts. Deduction theorem, completeness theorem, compactness theorem, non-standard models of arithmetic, elementary structures, chains.

name: Advanced Logic II
description: Formal number theory, primitive recursive and recursive functions, arithmetization, MRDP theorem, Godel incompleteness theorems, recursive undecidability, Church's theorem, Turing machines, partial recursive functions, unsolvable problems, Kleene-Mostowski hierarchy, effective computability, decision problems.

name: Ethics
description: The examination of major ethical systems. Teleological and deontological theories, existentialism, etc.

name: Social & Political Philosophy
description: A systematic study of fundamental explanations and concepts concerning human society and political institutions; distributive justice, equality, sovereignty, law, liberty and political obligations.

name: Philosophy of Language
description: An examination of the nature and structure of language and of philosophical problems arising in connection with it. Topics covered will include meaning, reference, speech acts and relevant issues of contemporary descriptive linguistics.

name: Philosophy of Mind
description: Investigation of some of the following topics: the mind-body problems, personal identity, the unity of consciousness, the unconscious, the problem of other minds, action, intention, and will.

name: Ontology
description: The concept of object, event and existence. The condition and ultimate units of existence.

name: Current Issues in Philosophy
description: This course will involve a thorough discussion of a variety of current problems to be selected among philosophical issues such as the theory of identity, essentialism, subject-predicate distinction, prescriptivism, causality, etc.

name: The Self
description: Philosophical examination of the self or ego or I as both subject and object in philosophy. Study of such questions as self-reference and indexicality, self-knowledge, the nature of the self, sympathy and identification with others in art and culture, isolation and social alienation from others, plasticity and historical constitution of the self, and the varieties of transcendence of the ego in ethics.

name: History of Islamic Thought
description: Conceptual frameworks of Islamic philosophy. The relations between Aristotelian, neo-Platonic and Islamic philosophy with respect to ontological and epistemological questions.

name: History of Political Thought II
description: Analysis of the works of the major Western political theorists from Machiavelli to the present, with emphasis on general developments, trends, and basic issues in modern political theory.

name: Comparative Politics
description: Major concepts and theoretical approaches in comparative politics. Comparative party systems, electoral systems, political institutions, state-society relations, democratization, and political culture.

name: Diplomatic History
description: History of diplomacy and international relations from the French Revolution to the end of the Cold War. The emergence of balance of power systems, nationalism, colonialism, the World Wars, decolonization and the Cold War.

name: Introduction to International Relations
description: The rise and evolution of the nation-state system, the operation of balance of power, deterrence, coercion, conflict, diplomacy, crisis management, and the role of international law and institutions in inter-state relations.

name: Introduction to Turkish Politics
description: The development of the Turkish political system from the Ottoman period to the present with emphasis on the interaction of state, politics, and society.

name: Fundamentals of Political Economy
description: An introduction to the basic concepts, theories and methodologies of political economy. The interaction between states and markets and between power and wealth at domestic and international contexts.

name: Development of Contemporary Democracies
description: Examination of the historical origins and development of democracy in a comparative perspective, with emphasis on major historical processes and contemporary debates.

name: Politics of Nationalism & Ethnicity
description: Nationalism and nation-building in historical perspective. Ethnicity, national consciousness, and ethnic nationalism in an international and comparative framework.

name: Contemporary Political Ideologies
description: Study of liberalism, conservatism, socialism, communism, social democracy, nationalism, from their origins in the 18th century to the present.

name: Secularism and Its Critiques
description: The etymological, philosophical, scientific and historical origins of secularism. A survey of the contemporary political philosophical critiques of secularism.

name: Politics in Developing Countries
description: The structures and processes of politics in developing countries with special attention on the dynamics of regime changes.

name: Political Economy of Contemporary Turkey
description: Comprehensive examination of the political economy of contemporary Turkey, with particular emphasis on the changing role of the state in the development process.

name: Politics of Latin America
description: The structures and political processes in Latin American countries with a focus on populism, revolution, authoritarianism, and democracy. Historical and theoretical examination of political change and economic development in the region.

name: Politics and Society in the Middle East
description: A general introduction to histories, peoples and politics of the Middle East. Colonialism, imperialism, orientalism, state, institutions, popular culture, nationalism, democratization, political Islam, patriarchy, social movements.

name: Theories of International Relations
description: Contending theories of international relations. Realism, neorealism, theories of integration and interdependence, constructivism, postmodernist and feminist approaches.

name: Twentieth Century Diplomatic History
description: In depth coverage of twentieth century diplomatic history. Causes and consequences of the two world wars, the emergence of the bipolar system, post-Cold War developments and conflicts.

name: Environment and Politics
description: Political development and dynamics of environmental issues, with reference to both domestic and international contexts. Green movement and its implications for post-industrial politics.

name: Political Sociology
description: Development of the modern state, the relationship of the state to society, with special emphasis on the nature of modern political institutions and processes.

name: Selected Issues in the History of Political Thought
description: Comprehensive analysis of the genesis and historical evolution of selected political concepts and controversies. Selected political thinkers and the in-depth appraisal of their contribution to political thought.

name: Foreign Policy
description: Foreign policy making processes and analyses. Politics and foreign policy. Actors, interests and interactions.

name: American Government
description: Survey of contemporary US government, with emphasis on the functioning of the federal system, the powers of the presidency, Congress, and the Supreme Court.

name: Introduction to European Integration
description: A study of the evolution of the European integration project from the European Coal and Steel Community to the present European Union, with emphasis on the politics of the deepening of integration and the expansion of EU membership.

name: Middle East in World Politics
description: Historical evolution of the modern Middle East since the decline of the Ottoman Empire. Fundamental issues of the Middle East in contemporary world politics.

name: Problems & Issues in Turkish Politics
description: Discussion of current issues in Turkish political life with special emphasis on secularism, civil-military relations, and problems of democracy.

name: Communications & Politics
description: The global revolution in mass communication and its impact on political processes, cultural identity, national and global issues.

name: Democratic Theory
description: Contextual survey of the development of democratic theory since Hobbes, with special emphasis on contemporary problems.

name: Contemporary American Politics
description: Social, economic, and political changes in the U.S.A. since World War II. The impact of technological change and global economic system on American politics.

name: Political Behavior
description: Impact of psychological, cultural and social structural factors on individual and mass behavior in political life, with emphasis on voting behavior.

name: Political Psychology
description: Introduction to the theories and empirical findings on political cognition, attitudes, values and beliefs. Theories of political socialization, political action, and protest behavior.

name: From Weimar to Berlin
description: Analysis of social and political problems leading to the collapse of the Weimar Republic, rise and fall of the Third Reich, the establishment of the Federal Republic, and German Unification.

name: International Political Economy
description: The interdependence of economic and political factors at the international level with special emphasis on the politicization of international economic relations.

name: Comparative State & Bureaucracy
description: Typologies of states and bureaucracies with particular emphasis on the relationship in different political systems.

name: Social Movements
description: Exploring various dimensions and modalities of human deprivation and exclusion. Study of linkages between globalization and exclusion, various theories on marginality, poverty, informality and inequality, analysis of political solutions and strategies.

name: Political Economy of Exclusion
description: Introduction to the theory of social movements. Case studies of old and new types of social movements in a comparative perspective.

name: Issues in Turkish Foreign Policy
description: Major issues in Turkey's foreign relations, regional problems and involvement. Evolution of Turkey's foreign policy goals.

name: Current Issues in World Politics
description: Current developments in issues and problem areas of international politics.

name: Migrants, Refugees and Politics: Comparative Perspectives
description: Analysis of the past and present of transnational migratory movements; selected case studies including Turkey and the EU; comparison of different migration and asylum policies and their social and political impact on destination countiries.

name: Peace and Conflict
description: Survey of psychological, social, political and religious factors shaping conflict. Analyses of theories of peace, peacebuilding, and reconciliation.

name: The Law of International Institutions
description: Development and nature of the principles, structures, and legal processes of international institutions, with special emphasis on the United Nations.

name: Human Rights: Theory & Practice
description: Theoretical foundations and historical development of human rights. Evolution of international human rights regimes and their impact on international and domestic politics.

name: Populism and Democracy
description: A comparative study of populist and Bonapartist politics in democracies from a historical perspective.
